using word parts, what does tachypnea most likely mean? ( -pnea = breathing) slow breathing absence of breathing rapid breathing difficult breathing tachy- means fast and -pnea means breathing, so tachypnea = rapid breathing. slow breathing is bradypnea, and absence of breathing is apnea ( a- = without).

what does the prefix in antibacterial mean? before between against without anti- means against: antibacterial = working against bacteria. before is pre- or ante- , between is inter- and without is a- or an- .
a neurologist is a specialist in the: kidneys blood skin nervous system neur- means nerve, and -ologist means one who studies or specializes. kidneys = nephr-, blood = hem- or hemat-, skin = derm-.

read the sentence and use context clues. the cut was so superficial that it affected only the top layer of skin and did not need stitches. what does superficial most nearly mean? very deep on the surface infected painful the clue "affected only the top layer of skin" tells you the cut stayed on the surface. a deep cut would usually need stitches, so "very deep" contradicts the sentence.

the usually taciturn patient surprised the nurses by chatting for an hour about his grandchildren. based on the context, what does taciturn most nearly mean? quiet and reserved cheerful and friendly confused and forgetful angry and impatient the word "surprised" signals a contrast: chatting for an hour was unusual for him. so taciturn must mean the opposite of talkative: quiet and reserved. cheerful, confused and angry don't create the contrast with chatting that the sentence sets up.

read the sentence and use context clues. the patient was lethargic ; he slept most of the day and barely responded when spoken to. what does lethargic most nearly mean? excited and restless in severe pain very hungry sluggish and drowsy the semicolon introduces an explanation: sleeping most of the day and barely responding describe someone sluggish and drowsy. nothing in the sentence mentions pain, hunger or restlessness.

read the sentence and use context clues. the nurse tried to alleviate the patient's anxiety by explaining each step of the procedure and holding her hand. what does alleviate most nearly mean? increase ignore measure relieve explaining each step and holding her hand are comforting actions, so the nurse is trying to reduce, or relieve, the anxiety. a nurse would not try to increase or ignore anxiety with comforting actions.

read the sentences and use context clues. the new medication proved highly efficacious . the patient's symptoms disappeared within two days, and the doctor began prescribing it to other patients. what does efficacious most nearly mean? expensive dangerous effective experimental the symptoms disappeared and the doctor wanted to use it again, so the medicine worked well. nothing in the sentences mentions cost or danger, and a medicine that has "proved" itself is no longer just experimental.

the prefix peri- means "around." what is the pericardium ? the sac that surrounds the heart the inner lining of the heart a single heart muscle cell a blood vessel leaving the heart peri- (around) + cardi (heart) = the membrane sac around the heart. the inner lining of the heart is the endocardium ( endo- = within).
type the suffix that means "surgical removal," as in tonsillectomy and mastectomy . (you do not need to type the hyphen.) -ectomy means surgical removal. tonsill + ectomy = removal of the tonsils.

type the root that means "skin," as in dermatitis and epidermis . (you do not need to type the hyphen.) derm- (also written derma- or dermat- ) means skin. the epidermis is the outer layer of skin ( epi- = upon).

which terms describe a condition that is below normal? select all that apply. hypothermia hypotension hyperglycemia hypokalemia tachycardia hypo- means below normal: low body temperature (hypothermia), low blood pressure (hypotension) and low blood potassium (hypokalemia). hyper glycemia is high blood sugar, and tachy cardia is a fast heart rate.

which words contain a prefix meaning "not" or "without"? select all that apply. atypical unconscious preoperative nonsterile postpartum a- (without), un- (not) and non- (not) are negative prefixes: atypical, unconscious, nonsterile. pre- means before and post- means after.

click the word part that means "inflammation." the suffix -itis means inflammation (tonsillitis, appendicitis, arthritis). gastr- means stomach and enter- means intestine. gastroenteritis is inflammation of the stomach and intestines, often called the "stomach flu."

a hypodermic needle goes under the skin. click the word part that means "under." the prefix hypo- means under or below normal (hypothermia, hypoglycemia). derm means skin, and -ic means "related to." its opposite is hyper- , meaning above or more than normal.

read the sentence. before the patient goes home, the nurse will dress the wound on his leg. as used in this sentence, what does dress mean? put clothing on decorate or arrange clean and cover with a bandage prepare by adding a sauce "dress" has several meanings. here its object is "the wound," so it means to clean and apply a bandage (a dressing).

read the sentence. after a night of close monitoring, the patient's condition is stable . as used in this sentence, what does stable mean? not changing much or getting worse a building where horses are kept firmly fixed so it will not tip over calm and cheerful in health care, a stable condition is steady: vital signs are not changing much and the patient is not getting worse.

the prefix trans- appears in transport and transfer . based on its meaning, what is a transcontinental railroad? a railroad that runs across a continent a railroad that runs under a continent a railroad within a single city a railroad that runs again after repairs trans- means across or through. to transport is to carry across, and a transcontinental railroad goes across a continent.

read the sentence. the lab will grow a culture from the throat swab to check for strep bacteria. as used in this sentence, what does culture mean? the shared beliefs and customs of a group appreciation of art, music, and literature a sample of microorganisms grown in a lab the way a workplace usually operates the clues "lab," "grow," "throat swab," and "bacteria" point to the science meaning: microorganisms grown on purpose so they can be identified.

use context clues to choose the meaning of benign . the biopsy showed the lump was benign , so the family was relieved that no further treatment was needed. cancerous not harmful painful growing quickly the family was relieved and no treatment was needed, so benign means not harmful.

read the sentence. before your shift starts, check with the charge nurse for your patient assignments. as used in this sentence, what does charge mean? the price that a business asks for a service responsible for running the unit a formal accusation that someone broke a law stored electrical energy, as in a battery the charge nurse is the nurse in charge of the unit for that shift, which is why that person hands out assignments.

use context clues. unlike her gregarious roommate, who loved parties and chatting with strangers, lena preferred quiet evenings alone. what does gregarious mean? shy sociable organized forgetful "unlike" signals contrast. lena likes quiet evenings, and the roommate loves parties and chatting, so gregarious means sociable.

the prefix inter- means "between," and intra- means "within." what is an intramural basketball league? a league of games played between different schools a league of games played within one school a league for players outside of school a league that plays only after school intra- means within, and -mural comes from the latin word for wall. an intramural league stays within one school's walls. games between different schools would be interscholastic or intercollegiate.

in which sentences does discharge mean "fluid that comes out of the body"? select all that apply. the patient's discharge is scheduled for 2 p.m. the wound had a small amount of yellow discharge. the nurse reviewed the discharge instructions with the family. the child had a fever and discharge draining from her ear. the provider noted clear nasal discharge. in the wound, ear, and nasal sentences, discharge is fluid coming from the body. in the other two, discharge means release from the hospital.
which word means "able to be used again"? useless misused reusable unusable re- (again) + use + -able (able to be) = reusable.

which phrase is redundant (says the same thing twice)? past history medical history recent visit daily dose history is always in the past, so "past history" repeats itself. the other phrases each add new information.

which revision is most concise? "due to the fact that the clinic was closed, we went to urgent care." because the clinic was closed, we went to urgent care. due to the fact of the clinic being closed, we went to urgent care. in light of the fact that the clinic was closed, we went to urgent care. owing to the fact that the clinic was closed, we went to urgent care. "due to the fact that" is a wordy way to say because . the other choices just swap in different wordy phrases.

which sentence has no redundant words? the nurse repeated the instructions again. the nurse repeated the instructions over again. the nurse repeated the instructions. the nurse repeated and restated the instructions again. repeat already means "say again," so adding again or over again is redundant.

which revision is the most concise? "at this point in time, the doctor is with another patient." at this point in time, the doctor is currently with another patient. the doctor is with another patient now. at this present time, the doctor is with another patient. at the current point in time, the doctor is now with another patient. "at this point in time" means now . the other choices keep the wordy phrase or add more repetition (currently, now).

which sentence is clear, with no ambiguous pronoun? ana told maria that she needed to update the chart. when ana called maria, she was at the pharmacy. ana and maria met before she left for her shift. ana told maria, “i need to update the chart.” in the other choices, she could mean ana or maria. quoting ana's words makes it clear that ana is the one who needs to update the chart.

which revision makes this sentence clear? "the nurse put the medication on the tray and then cleaned it." the nurse put the medication on the tray and then cleaned it off. the nurse put the medication on the tray and then cleaned the tray. the nurse put the medication on the tray and then cleaned it thoroughly. the nurse put the medication on the tray, and then it was cleaned. in the original, it could mean the medication or the tray. replacing it with the noun ( the tray ) removes the confusion. the other choices still use the unclear it .

choose the most precise word to complete the sentence. the patient's temperature ______ from 98.6 °f to 103 °f in two hours. rose changed went happened rose tells the reader exactly which way the temperature moved: up. changed and went are vague, and happened does not make sense.

which instruction is the most precise? take some tablets every so often. take a couple of tablets a few times a day. take 2 tablets every 6 hours with water. take the tablets regularly. precise writing gives exact numbers and times: 2 tablets, every 6 hours. vague words such as some , a couple , a few and regularly could lead to a dosing error.

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. the clinic saw ______ patients this week than last week. less lesser littler fewer use fewer for things you can count (patients) and less for amounts you measure (less water, less time).

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. from the doctor's smile, the patient ______ that the news was good. inferred implied implicated inflected to infer is to draw a conclusion from clues; the listener infers. to imply is to hint; the speaker implies. here the patient is drawing the conclusion.

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. the clinic accepts all insurance plans ______ one. accept expect excess except except means "other than" or "leaving out." accept means to receive, expect means to anticipate and excess means too much.

which is the most concise version of this sentence? "the reason why she was late is because the bus was delayed." she was late because the bus was delayed. the reason why she was late is that the bus was delayed. the reason she was late is due to the fact that the bus was delayed. the reason why is because she was late since the bus was delayed. "the reason why ... is because" says the same thing three times (reason, why, because). start with the subject and verb, then give the cause: "she was late because ..."

which single word best replaces very tired to make this sentence more precise? after a 12-hour night shift, the nurse was very tired. sleepy drowsy exhausted bored exhausted means extremely tired, so it replaces both words with one strong word. sleepy and drowsy mean wanting to sleep, not extreme tiredness, and bored means something else.

which sentence is free of redundancy? each patient received a free gift. each patient received a sample of lotion. the final outcome of the study was positive. the nurses will meet together at 3 p.m. a gift is already free, an outcome is already final, and meet already means come together. "a sample of lotion" has no repeated meaning.

which sentence is the clearest and most direct? the medication was given to the patient at noon by the nurse. at noon, there was the giving of medication by the nurse to the patient. the nurse gave the patient her medication at noon. it was at noon that the medication was what the nurse gave to the patient. active voice (subject → action → receiver) is usually the clearest: "the nurse gave ..." the passive version is grammatical but wordier, and the last two choices are awkward and hard to follow.

which revision removes the wordiness from this sentence? "in order to apply, you need to fill out the form in its entirety." in order to apply, you need to complete the form in its entirety. to apply, complete the entire form. to apply, you need to fill out the form in its entirety completely. in order for you to apply, fill out the entire whole form. "in order to" can be shortened to to , and "fill out ... in its entirety" can be shortened to complete the entire form . the other choices keep the wordy phrases or add redundancy (entirety completely, entire whole).

which phrases are redundant? select all that apply. end result advance planning free gift blood test annual checkup a result comes at the end, planning is done in advance, and a gift is free, so these phrases repeat themselves. "blood test" and "annual checkup" each add information.

which sentences contain an ambiguous pronoun? select all that apply. when the doctor spoke with the patient, he seemed worried. carlos called his mother after his shift ended. take the cap off the bottle and throw it away. the nurses told the students that they would be late. the pharmacist checked the label before she filled the prescription. ambiguous: he (doctor or patient?), it (cap or bottle?) and they (nurses or students?). clear: carlos is the only person who can own the mother and the shift, and the pharmacist is the only person in the last sentence.

which word has the most positive connotation for describing a patient who asks many questions about her care? nosy demanding engaged pushy engaged suggests the patient is interested and involved in her care, which is positive. nosy , demanding and pushy all have negative connotations.

which choice combines these sentences most concisely? the clinic is in merced. the clinic offers free flu shots. the flu shots are offered on saturdays. the clinic is in merced, and the clinic offers free flu shots, and they are on saturdays. in merced is the clinic, which offers flu shots that are free and that are on saturdays. the clinic, which is in merced, offers flu shots, which are free, which are on saturdays. the clinic in merced offers free flu shots on saturdays. combine the details into one subject and one verb: "the clinic in merced offers free flu shots on saturdays." the other choices repeat words or stack clauses.

which revision replaces the vague word stuff with precise language? "bring your stuff to the appointment." bring your things to the appointment. bring all your stuff and things to the appointment. bring whatever you need to the appointment. bring your insurance card and medication list to the appointment. precise language names exactly what to bring. things and whatever you need are as vague as stuff .

which sentence uses standard english word choice? irregardless of the heat, the clinic stayed open. regardless of the heat, the clinic stayed open. the heat could of caused her dizziness. she was laying on the couch all afternoon. regardless is standard; "irregardless" is nonstandard (the ir- and -less both mean "not"). "could of" should be could have , and a person reclining is lying , not "laying."

click the word that is used incorrectly. effect is usually a noun: a result. affect is usually a verb: to influence. after "a strong," the sentence needs a noun, so it should be effect . memory trick: a ffect is an a ction; e ffect is the e nd result.

click the word that is used incorrectly. lie means to recline (you lie down). lay means to put something down, and it needs an object (lay the tray on the table). the patient is reclining, not placing an object, so the sentence needs lie down. advised is correct here: it is the verb. (advice is the noun.)

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. the urgent care clinic is usually busier on mondays ______ on fridays. then than that as than is used to compare (busier than). then tells about time (first this, then that).
choose the correct word. please ______ your hands before entering the room. wash was washes wish "please wash" is a command; the base verb fits.
which word best completes the sentence? the nurse spoke in a ______ voice to calm the frightened child. harsh soothing loud sarcastic to calm a frightened child, a soothing voice makes sense.

which sentence uses accept or except correctly? everyone except jamal finished the quiz. the clinic does not except walk-ins. please except my apology. everyone accept jamal finished the quiz. "except" means excluding; "accept" means to receive or agree to.

which revision makes the sentence most precise? "the patient took some medicine a while ago." the patient took some medicine earlier today. the patient took 500 mg of acetaminophen at 2:00 p.m. the patient took a pill sometime. the patient took some stuff for her pain a little while ago. precise writing gives specific details: what, how much, and when.
which word has the most negative connotation? thrifty economical stingy careful with money all four describe spending little, but "stingy" suggests selfishness, which gives it a negative connotation.

choose the word that best completes the sentence. the results were ______: two tests showed improvement and one did not. conclusive mixed identical unanimous some tests improved and one didn't, so the results were mixed.
choose the correct word. the bandage was too ______, so the nurse loosened it. lose loose tight tite if the nurse loosened it, it was too tight.

which sentence uses adverse or averse correctly? the patient had an averse reaction to penicillin. he is adverse to taking pills, so he asked for a liquid. the new medication has few adverse effects. the family was adverse to the idea of moving her. adverse means harmful or unfavorable, as in an adverse reaction or adverse effects. averse means unwilling or opposed, describing a person's feelings: averse to taking pills.

which revision removes the redundancy? "the final outcome of the study was surprising." the final end outcome of the study was surprising. the outcome of the study was surprising. the final outcome result was surprising. the study's final ending outcome was surprising. an outcome is already final, so "final outcome" is redundant.

which decimal is equal to 3/8? 0.125 0.375 0.0375 2.667 a fraction bar means divide: 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. 2.667 comes from dividing the wrong way (8 ÷ 3). 0.0375 has the decimal point one place too far left, and 0.125 is only 1/8, not 3/8.

a patient's chart says 0.45 of the meal tray was eaten. what is 0.45 written as a percent? 45% 450% 0.45% 4.5% to change a decimal to a percent, multiply by 100 (move the decimal point 2 places right). 0.45 × 100 = 45, so 0.45 = 45%. 4.5% and 450% move the decimal the wrong number of places; 0.45% does not move it at all.
write 72% as a decimal. percent means "per hundred," so divide by 100. 72 ÷ 100 = 0.72 (move the decimal point 2 places left).

which improper fraction is equal to 2 1/4? 8/4 3/4 6/4 9/4 multiply the whole number by the denominator, then add the numerator: 2 × 4 + 1 = 9. keep the same denominator: 2 1/4 = 9/4. 8/4 forgets to add the 1, and 6/4 multiplies 2 × 1 before adding 4.

which of these values is the greatest? 0.6 5/8 0.615 62% change everything to decimals: 5/8 = 0.625, 62% = 0.62, 0.6 = 0.600, 0.615 = 0.615. compare place by place: 0.625 > 0.620 > 0.615 > 0.600. 62% looks big because 62 is a large number, but as a decimal it is 0.62, which is less than 0.625.

which values are equivalent to 3/5? select all that apply. 0.6 0.35 60% 9/15 5/3 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6, and 0.6 × 100 = 60%. 9/15 simplifies to 3/5 when you divide the top and bottom by 3. 0.35 just writes the digits 3 and 5 after a decimal point, and 5/3 flips the fraction (it is about 1.67).

put these numbers in order from least to greatest. 0.09 1/8 0.2 23% 1/4 convert to decimals: 0.09, 1/8 = 0.125, 0.2 = 0.20, 23% = 0.23, 1/4 = 0.25. line up the decimal places: 0.090 < 0.125 < 0.200 < 0.230 < 0.250. watch out for 0.09: it is less than 0.2 even though 9 is bigger than 2, because 0.09 means 9 hundredths.

a patient finished 2/3 of a bottle of a nutrition shake. about what percent of the shake did the patient drink? round to the nearest whole percent. 150% 66% 67% 23% 2 ÷ 3 = 0.6666…, and 0.6666… × 100 = 66.66…%. the digit after the 6 in the ones place is 6, so round up: about 67%. 66% chops off the decimals instead of rounding, 23% just writes the digits 2 and 3, and 150% comes from 3 ÷ 2.
write 0.875 as a fraction in lowest terms. (type it like 3/4.) 0.875 is 875 thousandths: 875/1000. divide the top and bottom by 125: 875 ÷ 125 = 7 and 1000 ÷ 125 = 8. so 0.875 = 7/8.

a medicated cream is 1.5% hydrocortisone. what is 1.5% written as a decimal? 0.015 0.0015 0.15 1.5 divide by 100: move the decimal point 2 places to the left. 1.5 → 0.15 → 0.015. 0.15 moves only one place, and 0.0015 moves three places.

which fraction is between 1/2 and 3/4? 5/8 7/8 4/5 3/8 write all of them in eighths or as decimals: 1/2 = 0.5 and 3/4 = 0.75. 5/8 = 0.625, which is between 0.5 and 0.75. 3/8 = 0.375 is too small; 7/8 = 0.875 and 4/5 = 0.8 are too large.

which list shows the numbers in order from least to greatest ? 0.7, 7/9, 72%, 3/4 72%, 0.7, 7/9, 3/4 0.7, 72%, 3/4, 7/9 7/9, 3/4, 72%, 0.7 convert: 0.7 = 0.700, 72% = 0.720, 3/4 = 0.750, 7/9 ≈ 0.778. least to greatest: 0.700, 0.720, 0.750, 0.778. the list starting with 7/9 is greatest to least (backwards). putting 7/9 second treats it as smaller than it is: 7 ÷ 9 ≈ 0.778.
which fraction is equal to 0.3? 1/3 3/100 30/10 3/10 0.3 means 3 tenths, so it is 3/10. 1/3 is 0.333…, which is close but not equal. 3/100 is 0.03, and 30/10 is 3.

an almond grower in madera county has harvested 18 of the 24 rows in an orchard. what percent of the rows have been harvested? 75% 18% 25% 133% percent harvested = part ÷ whole × 100 = 18 ÷ 24 × 100. 18 ÷ 24 = 0.75, and 0.75 × 100 = 75%. 25% is the percent not harvested. 133% comes from dividing 24 ÷ 18 (whole ÷ part).

write 5/12 as a decimal rounded to the nearest hundredth. 4.17 0.42 0.41 2.40 5 ÷ 12 = 0.41666… to round to the hundredths place, look at the thousandths digit: it is 6, so round the 1 up to 2. the answer is 0.42. 0.41 truncates instead of rounding, 2.40 is 12 ÷ 5, and 4.17 has the decimal point in the wrong place.

what is 3/20 written as a percent? 1.5% 0.15% 60% 15% make the denominator 100: multiply top and bottom by 5 → 3/20 = 15/100. 15/100 = 15%. 0.15% and 1.5% misplace the decimal, and 60% multiplies 3 × 20 instead of dividing.

a nurse sets a fluid goal of 2 1/2 liters for a patient. by noon the patient has had 1.75 l. what percent of the goal has the patient reached? change the mixed number to a decimal: 2 1/2 = 2.5 l. part ÷ whole = 1.75 ÷ 2.5 = 0.7. 0.7 × 100 = 70%.

which decimal is equal to 7/25? 3.57 0.07 0.725 0.28 multiply the top and bottom by 4 to get a denominator of 100: 7/25 = 28/100. 28/100 = 0.28. 3.57 is 25 ÷ 7 (upside down), 0.725 just strings the digits together, and 0.07 ignores the 25.
write 0.6 as a percent. multiply by 100: 0.6 × 100 = 60. so 0.6 = 60%. (it is not 6%; 0.6 means 6 tenths, which is 60 hundredths.)

which values are greater than 2/3? select all that apply. 0.7 0.66 69% 13/20 5/7 2/3 = 0.666…, so compare each value to 0.667. 0.7, 69% = 0.69, and 5/7 ≈ 0.714 are all greater. 0.66 is a trap: 0.660 is less than 0.666…. 13/20 = 0.65 is also less.

which mixed number is equal to 11/4? 2 1/4 3 3/4 2 3/4 3 1/4 divide: 11 ÷ 4 = 2 with a remainder of 3. the remainder becomes the new numerator: 11/4 = 2 3/4. check: 2 × 4 + 3 = 11. the other choices give 9/4, 13/4, and 15/4.

each small tick mark on the number line is 1/4. click the point that shows 3/4. 3/4 = 0.75, which is three small ticks to the right of 0. point b is at −3/4 (to the left of 0). watch the sign. point d is 1 1/2 and point e is 2 1/4.
write 3/8 as a decimal. divide the top by the bottom: 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375.
which value is the largest? 0.6 5/8 0.59 3/5 convert to decimals: 0.6, 5/8 = 0.625, 0.59, 3/5 = 0.6. the largest is 0.625.
write 1.4 as a percent. (type a number only.) multiply by 100: 1.4 × 100 = 140%.
what is 2⅓ written as an improper fraction? 5/3 7/3 6/3 2/3 multiply the whole number by the denominator and add the numerator: 2 × 3 + 1 = 7. keep the denominator: 7/3.
calculate 2/3 + 3/4. type your answer as an improper fraction in lowest terms (like 5/4). common denominator 12: 2/3 = 8/12 and 3/4 = 9/12. 8/12 + 9/12 = 17/12.
what is 3/4 ÷ 1/2? 3/8 1 1/2 2/3 1/4 dividing by a fraction = multiplying by its reciprocal: 3/4 × 2/1 = 6/4 = 1 1/2.
a patient drank 2/3 of an 8-ounce cup of juice. how many ounces did the patient drink? 5 1/3 oz 6 oz 2 2/3 oz 5 oz 2/3 × 8 = 16/3 = 5 1/3 ounces.
on the number line, each small tick is 1/8. which letter marks 5/8? a b c d count eighths from 0: 1/8, 2/8, 3/8, 4/8 (= ½), 5/8. b is one tick past the ½ mark, which is 5/8 (0.625).
which number does point c represent? 1.2 1.25 1.4 0.25 c is two eighth-ticks past 1: 1 + 2/8 = 1 + 1/4. 1/4 = 0.25, so c = 1.25.

each small tick on the number line is 1/4. which letter marks −7/4? a b c d −7/4 = −1 3/4 = −1.75. start at −1 and move left 3 quarter-ticks: −1.25, −1.5, −1.75. that's b. c is −1.25 (only one quarter to the left of −1), a common slip when people move right from −2 instead.

evaluate: 8 + 4 × 3 20 36 96 15 multiplication comes before addition: 4 × 3 = 12. then add: 8 + 12 = 20. 36 works left to right ((8 + 4) × 3), which ignores the order of operations. 15 adds all three numbers, and 96 multiplies all three.

evaluate: 18 − 6 ÷ 3 + 2² 8 12 20 16 exponent first: 2² = 4. then divide: 6 ÷ 3 = 2. finally add and subtract left to right: 18 − 2 + 4 = 20. 8 comes from doing 18 − 6 first. 12 subtracts the 4 instead of adding it, and 16 forgets the + 4.
what is −7 + 12? −5 5 19 −19 the signs are different, so subtract the absolute values: 12 − 7 = 5. keep the sign of the number with the larger absolute value (12 is positive), so the answer is 5.
what is (−6)(−4)? 24 −10 −24 10 a negative times a negative is positive. 6 × 4 = 24, so (−6)(−4) = 24. −10 and 10 add the numbers instead of multiplying.
evaluate: −15 ÷ 3 − (−4) divide first: −15 ÷ 3 = −5. subtracting a negative is the same as adding: −5 − (−4) = −5 + 4. −5 + 4 = −1.

what is 3/4 + 2/3? 1 5/12 5/7 1 1/8 1/2 use a common denominator of 12: 3/4 = 9/12 and 2/3 = 8/12. 9/12 + 8/12 = 17/12 = 1 5/12. 5/7 adds the tops and the bottoms, which is never allowed. 1/2 multiplies the fractions, and 1 1/8 (9/8) divides them.

what is 2 1/2 × 1 1/3? 1 7/8 2 1/6 3 5/6 3 1/3 change to improper fractions: 2 1/2 = 5/2 and 1 1/3 = 4/3. multiply: 5/2 × 4/3 = 20/6 = 10/3 = 3 1/3. 2 1/6 multiplies the whole numbers and the fractions separately. 3 5/6 adds instead of multiplying, and 1 7/8 divides.

a patient's temperature is recorded as 99.368°f on a digital readout. what is this rounded to the nearest tenth? 99.4°f 99.37°f 99°f 99.3°f the tenths digit is 3. look at the digit to its right (the hundredths digit): 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round the 3 up to 4: 99.4°f. 99.37 rounds to the hundredth, and 99 rounds to the whole number.
round 0.04682 to the nearest hundredth. the hundredths digit is 4 (0.0 4 682). the next digit is 6, so round up: 0.04 → 0.05.

a bottle holds 4.2 oz of infant formula, and the baby drinks 1.75 oz. how much formula is left in the bottle? 3.45 oz 2.45 oz 5.95 oz 3.55 oz line up the decimal points and write 4.2 as 4.20. 4.20 − 1.75 = 2.45 oz. 3.55 subtracts the smaller digit from the larger in each place instead of borrowing, 3.45 subtracts only 0.75, and 5.95 adds instead of subtracting.

what is 0.6 × 0.04? 2.4 0.24 0.024 0.0024 multiply as whole numbers: 6 × 4 = 24. count the decimal places in the factors: 0.6 has 1 and 0.04 has 2, for a total of 3. put 3 decimal places in the answer: 0.024.
what is 3.6 ÷ 0.09? move both decimal points 2 places right so you divide by a whole number: 3.6 ÷ 0.09 = 360 ÷ 9. 360 ÷ 9 = 40. check: 40 × 0.09 = 3.6 ✓

evaluate: −2(5 − 9)² ÷ 4 + 3 11 −11 19 −5 parentheses: 5 − 9 = −4. exponent: (−4)² = 16 (a negative squared is positive). multiply and divide left to right: −2 × 16 = −32, then −32 ÷ 4 = −8. add: −8 + 3 = −5. choice 11 treats (−4)² as −16; 19 squares the −2 as well; −11 subtracts the 3.

which expressions are equal to −12? select all that apply. (−3)(4) −24 ÷ (−2) −20 + 8 −4 − (−8) 6 − 18 (−3)(4) = −12, −20 + 8 = −12, and 6 − 18 = −12. −24 ÷ (−2) = +12, because a negative divided by a negative is positive. −4 − (−8) = −4 + 8 = 4.
evaluate: 15 − 3 × 4 multiply first: 3 × 4 = 12. then subtract: 15 − 12 = 3. (working left to right would give 48, which is wrong.)

early on a winter morning near huntington lake in the sierra, the temperature was −6°f. by afternoon it had risen 23 degrees. what was the afternoon temperature? 29°f −29°f 17°f −17°f "risen" means add: −6 + 23. different signs: 23 − 6 = 17, and the larger number (23) is positive, so the answer is 17°f. −29 subtracts instead of adding, and 29 ignores the negative sign on −6.

evaluate (3/4 − 1/3) ÷ 5/8. write your answer as a fraction in lowest terms. parentheses first, with a denominator of 12: 9/12 − 4/12 = 5/12. to divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal: 5/12 × 8/5. 5/12 × 8/5 = 40/60 = 2/3.

a clinic's supply budget spreadsheet shows a cost of $18.4562 per box of gloves. what is this rounded to the nearest cent? $18.456 $18.46 $18.45 $18.50 the nearest cent is the hundredths place: $18.4 5 62. the next digit is 6, so round the 5 up: $18.46. $18.45 truncates, $18.50 rounds to the nearest dime, and $18.456 rounds to the thousandth.

which numbers are less than −1? select all that apply. −1.5 −0.9 −5/4 −1 −2.01 on a number line, "less than −1" means to the left of −1. −1.5, −5/4 (= −1.25), and −2.01 are all left of −1. −0.9 is to the right of −1 (closer to zero), and −1 is equal to −1, not less than it.

a student in merced has $45.20 in a checking account. she pays two bills of $62.75 and $18.30, then deposits $40.00. what is her balance now? −$4.15 −$35.85 $22.45 $4.15 write it as one expression: 45.20 − 62.75 − 18.30 + 40.00. 45.20 − 62.75 = −17.55; −17.55 − 18.30 = −35.85; −35.85 + 40.00 = 4.15. −$35.85 forgets the deposit, and $22.45 forgets the second bill.

put these numbers in order from least to greatest. −2.5 −1 3/4 −1.2 0.4 3/2 convert: −1 3/4 = −1.75 and 3/2 = 1.5. the most negative number is the least: −2.5 < −1.75 < −1.2. then the positives: 0.4 < 1.5.

a recipe needs 1/2 cup of oil per batch. how many batches can be made with 6.5 cups of oil? 7 13 6 3.25 number of batches = 6.5 ÷ 1/2. dividing by 1/2 is the same as multiplying by 2: 6.5 × 2 = 13. 3.25 multiplies by 1/2 instead of dividing.

click the point that is closest to the value of √5. √4 = 2 and √9 = 3, so √5 is between 2 and 3, a bit above 2. the on-screen calculator gives √5 ≈ 2.236. point e is at 2 1/4 = 2.25, the closest point.
evaluate: 8 + 12 ÷ 4 × 2 do multiplication and division left to right first: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, then 3 × 2 = 6. then add: 8 + 6 = 14.
evaluate: (3 + 5)² − 4 × 6 parentheses: 8. exponent: 64. multiply: 4 × 6 = 24. subtract: 64 − 24 = 40.
what is (−6) × (−4) ÷ 3? −8 8 −2 72 a negative times a negative is positive: 24. then 24 ÷ 3 = 8.
evaluate: 18 − 2(5 − 8)² inside parentheses: 5 − 8 = −3. square: 9. multiply: 2 × 9 = 18. subtract: 18 − 18 = 0.
which property is shown? 4 × (3 + 5) = 4 × 3 + 4 × 5 commutative associative distributive identity multiplying a number across a sum is the distributive property.
which is equivalent to 5³? 15 125 25 53 5³ = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125.
round 0.0467 to the nearest hundredth. 0.04 0.05 0.047 0.1 the hundredths digit is 4; the next digit (6) is 5 or more, so round up to 0.05.

according to the graph, how many degrees did the temperature rise from 6 a.m. to 3 p.m.? rise = later temperature − earlier temperature = 15 − (−3). subtracting a negative is adding: 15 + 3 = 18 degrees.

using the register, what was the account balance right after the scrubs and shoes were bought on 3/2? −$27.35 $27.35 $198.15 −$198.15 85.40 − 112.75: the purchase is bigger than the balance, so the result is negative. 112.75 − 85.40 = 27.35, so the balance is −$27.35 (overdrawn). that's why an overdraft fee shows up later.

what is the balance at the end of the register (after the 3/6 overdraft fee)? write it in dollars and cents. add the deposits and subtract the charges in order: 85.40 − 112.75 = −27.35. −27.35 + 436.20 = 408.85. then 408.85 − 115.00 = 293.85. then 293.85 − 35.00 = 258.85.

using the table, what is the difference in elevation between the highest and lowest points in california? 14,223 ft 14,787 ft 14,505 ft 13,941 ft write the low point as a negative number: −282 ft. difference = 14,505 − (−282) = 14,505 + 282 = 14,787 ft.
using clark's rule, what dose should a 60-lb child get if the adult dose is 500 mg? divide first: 60 ÷ 150 = 0.4. then multiply: 0.4 × 500 = 200 mg.

on a night shift, a hospital unit has 4 nurses for 28 patients. what is the ratio of nurses to patients in simplest form? 4:7 1:24 1:7 7:1 write nurses first: 4:28. divide both parts by 4: 4 ÷ 4 = 1 and 28 ÷ 4 = 7, so the ratio is 1:7. 7:1 reverses the order (patients to nurses). 1:24 subtracts instead of dividing.

a recipe uses 3 cups of flour to make 2 dozen tortillas. how many cups of flour are needed for 5 dozen tortillas? 3.33 7.5 6 15 set up a proportion: 3 cups / 2 dozen = x cups / 5 dozen. cross-multiply: 2x = 3 × 5 = 15, so x = 7.5 cups. 3.33 flips the ratio (2/3 × 5). 6 adds 3 extra cups for 3 extra dozen instead of scaling, and 15 forgets to divide by 2.
solve the proportion: x/12 = 15/36 cross-multiply: 36x = 12 × 15 = 180. divide: x = 180 ÷ 36 = 5. or notice 15/36 = 5/12, so x = 5.

a drive from fresno to bakersfield covers 110 miles and takes 1 hour 50 minutes. what is the average speed in miles per hour? 55 mph 73.3 mph 60 mph 1 mph change the time to hours: 50 minutes = 50/60 = 5/6 hour, so 1 hour 50 min = 1 5/6 = 11/6 hours. speed = distance ÷ time = 110 ÷ 11/6 = 110 × 6/11 = 60 mph. 73.3 mph treats 1 hr 50 min as 1.5 hours. 55 mph rounds the time up to 2 hours, and 1 is miles per minute (110 mi ÷ 110 min).

a visalia grocery store sells orange juice in two sizes: a 64-oz bottle for $5.12 and a 48-oz bottle for $4.08. which statement is correct? the 48-oz bottle is the better buy at $0.085 per ounce. the 64-oz bottle is the better buy at $0.125 per ounce. the 64-oz bottle is the better buy at $0.08 per ounce. both bottles cost the same amount per ounce. unit price = price ÷ ounces. 64 oz: $5.12 ÷ 64 = $0.08 per oz. 48 oz: $4.08 ÷ 48 = $0.085 per oz. the lower unit price ($0.08) is the better buy. $0.125 is not a price per ounce; 64 ÷ 5.12 = 12.5 is ounces per dollar.

on a road map, 1 inch represents 25 miles. fresno and merced are 2.4 inches apart on the map. about how many miles apart are they? 27.4 miles 60 miles 10.4 miles 0.096 miles multiply the map distance by the scale: 2.4 × 25 = 60 miles. 10.4 divides 25 by 2.4, 27.4 adds the numbers, and 0.096 divides 2.4 by 25.

an oral antibiotic suspension contains 250 mg in every 5 ml. the order is for 400 mg. how many ml should be given? set up the proportion: 250 mg / 5 ml = 400 mg / x ml. cross-multiply: 250x = 400 × 5 = 2,000. x = 2,000 ÷ 250 = 8 ml.

a farm crew picks 3 tons of grapes in 4 hours. at the same rate, how long will it take the crew to pick 7.5 tons? 5.6 hours 6 hours 8.5 hours 10 hours find the time per ton: 4 hours ÷ 3 tons = 4/3 hour per ton. 7.5 tons × 4/3 hour per ton = 10 hours. 5.6 hours multiplies by 3/4 (the flipped rate). 8.5 adds 4.5 more hours for 4.5 more tons, which is not proportional.
fill in the blank so the ratios are equal: 5 is to 8 as 15 is to ____. 15 is 3 times 5, so multiply 8 by 3 too. 8 × 3 = 24, so 5:8 = 15:24.

a teas prep class has 40 students. the ratio of men to women is 3:5. how many men are in the class? 15 25 24 8 the ratio 3:5 has 3 + 5 = 8 total parts. each part is 40 ÷ 8 = 5 students, so men = 3 × 5 = 15. 24 uses 3/5 of 40, treating 5 as the total. 25 is the number of women, and 8 is the number of parts.

which ratios are equivalent to 4:6? select all that apply. 2:3 6:9 6:4 10:15 5:7 4:6 simplifies to 2:3 (divide both by 2). 6:9 and 10:15 also simplify to 2:3 (divide by 3 and by 5). 6:4 reverses the order, and 5:7 adds 1 to each part, which does not keep the ratio the same.

an iv bag contains 2 g of a medication dissolved in 500 ml. how many milligrams of the medication are in 15 ml of this solution? 0.06 mg 60 mg 3,750 mg 6 mg convert grams to milligrams: 2 g = 2,000 mg. concentration: 2,000 mg ÷ 500 ml = 4 mg per ml. 15 ml × 4 mg/ml = 60 mg. 0.06 is the answer in grams, labeled as mg. 3,750 sets up the proportion upside down (500 × 15 ÷ 2).

a student nurse counts a patient's pulse at 18 beats in 15 seconds. what is the pulse rate in beats per minute? 72 33 36 270 there are four 15-second periods in 1 minute. 18 × 4 = 72 beats per minute. 36 multiplies by 2 (as if it were a 30-second count), 270 multiplies 18 × 15, and 33 adds.

which rates are equal to 60 miles per hour? select all that apply. 1 mile per minute 15 miles in 15 minutes 30 miles in 1 hour 90 miles in 1.5 hours 120 miles in 3 hours 60 miles per 60 minutes = 1 mile per minute, and 15 miles in 15 minutes is also 1 mile per minute. 90 miles ÷ 1.5 hours = 60 mph. 30 miles in 1 hour is 30 mph, and 120 miles ÷ 3 hours = 40 mph.

during a central valley heat wave, a farmworker is told to drink 8 oz of water every 15 minutes. how many ounces is that over a 6-hour shift? there are 60 ÷ 15 = 4 fifteen-minute periods in an hour. 4 × 8 oz = 32 oz per hour. 32 oz × 6 hours = 192 oz.

a rice recipe serves 6 people and uses 2/3 cup of uncooked rice. how much rice is needed to serve 15 people? 10 cups 2 1/2 cups 4/15 cup 1 2/3 cups scale factor: 15 ÷ 6 = 5/2. 2/3 × 5/2 = 10/6 = 5/3 = 1 2/3 cups. 4/15 uses the flipped factor 6/15. 10 cups multiplies 2/3 by 15 without dividing by 6, and 2 1/2 is just the scale factor.

it takes about 4.5 lb of fresh grapes to make 1 lb of raisins. how many pounds of fresh grapes are needed to make 30 lb of raisins? 34.5 lb 120 lb 6.7 lb 135 lb grapes : raisins = 4.5 : 1, so multiply by 30. 4.5 × 30 = 135 lb of grapes. 6.7 divides 30 by 4.5 (backwards), 34.5 adds, and 120 rounds 4.5 down to 4.

a car used 12 gallons of gas to drive 348 miles. at the same rate, how far can it go on 7 gallons? 341 miles 29 miles 203 miles 49.7 miles miles per gallon: 348 ÷ 12 = 29 mpg. 29 × 7 = 203 miles. 29 is only the first step (miles per gallon). 341 subtracts 7 from 348, and 49.7 divides 348 by 7.

a bag of 12 oranges costs $4.20. what is the cost per orange? $2.86 $50.40 $0.42 $0.35 unit price = total cost ÷ number of items. $4.20 ÷ 12 = $0.35 per orange. $2.86 divides 12 by 4.20, and $50.40 multiplies.

a cleaning solution for a clinic is mixed in a ratio of 1 part bleach to 9 parts water. how many milliliters of bleach are needed to make 2 l of solution? total parts = 1 + 9 = 10, and 2 l = 2,000 ml. bleach is 1 of the 10 parts: 2,000 ÷ 10 = 200 ml. a common mistake is 2,000 ÷ 9 ≈ 222 ml, which forgets that the water is only 9 of the 10 parts.

put these package sizes of almonds in order from the lowest cost per ounce to the highest cost per ounce. 24 oz for $4.56 16 oz for $3.20 32 oz for $6.72 10 oz for $2.30 divide price by ounces for each package. $4.56 ÷ 24 = $0.19; $3.20 ÷ 16 = $0.20; $6.72 ÷ 32 = $0.21; $2.30 ÷ 10 = $0.23. so the 24-oz bag is the best deal, and the 10-oz bag costs the most per ounce.

solve for x: 3/x = 9/21 7 63 15 27 cross-multiply: 9x = 3 × 21 = 63. x = 63 ÷ 9 = 7. 63 forgets to divide by 9. 27 multiplies 3 × 9, the wrong pair. 15 tries to subtract instead of using a proportion.
solve the proportion: 3/5 = x/40. what is x? cross-multiply: 5x = 3 × 40 = 120, so x = 24.
a recipe uses 2 cups of rice for 6 servings. how many cups are needed for 15 servings? 4 5 6 7.5 2/6 = x/15 → 6x = 30 → x = 5 cups.
an iv delivers 125 ml per hour. how many hours will it take to deliver 1,000 ml? 1,000 ml ÷ 125 ml/h = 8 hours.
the ratio of nurses to patients on a unit is 1:4. if there are 28 patients, how many nurses are needed? 4 7 24 112 28 ÷ 4 = 7 nurses.
a car travels 156 miles in 3 hours. at the same rate, how far will it go in 5 hours? 208 miles 260 miles 312 miles 234 miles rate = 156 ÷ 3 = 52 mph. 52 × 5 = 260 miles.
which unit rate is the best buy? 12 oz for $3.00 16 oz for $3.84 20 oz for $4.60 24 oz for $5.04 price per ounce: $0.25, $0.24, $0.23, $0.21. the 24 oz option is cheapest per ounce.
simplify the ratio 18:24. 3:4 6:8 9:12 2:3 divide both by the greatest common factor, 6: 3:4.

a provider orders 500 mg of a medication. each tablet contains 250 mg. how many tablets should the patient take? 2 tablets 0.5 tablet 4 tablets 1.5 tablets use desired ÷ have: 500 mg ÷ 250 mg per tablet = 2 tablets. check: 2 tablets × 250 mg = 500 mg, which matches the order. 0.5 tablet comes from dividing the wrong way (250 ÷ 500).

a child is ordered 375 mg of amoxicillin. the oral suspension contains 250 mg per 5 ml. how many milliliters should be given? use (desired ÷ have) × quantity: (375 mg ÷ 250 mg) × 5 ml. 375 ÷ 250 = 1.5, and 1.5 × 5 ml = 7.5 ml. check: the order is more than 250 mg, so the answer must be more than 5 ml.

digoxin 0.125 mg is ordered. the tablets on hand are 0.25 mg each. how many tablets should be given? ½ tablet 2 tablets 1 tablet ¼ tablet desired ÷ have: 0.125 mg ÷ 0.25 mg = 0.5, so give ½ tablet. the order is smaller than one tablet, so the answer must be less than 1. 2 tablets comes from dividing 0.25 by 0.125 (the wrong way).

heparin 5,000 units is ordered subcutaneously. the vial is labeled 10,000 units/ml. how many ml should be drawn up? 0.5 ml 2 ml 5 ml 0.05 ml desired ÷ have × quantity: (5,000 units ÷ 10,000 units) × 1 ml = 0.5 ml. the order is half the strength of 1 ml, so you need half a milliliter. 2 ml would be 20,000 units, four times the order. with a high-alert drug like heparin, always check that the answer makes sense.

a provider orders 60 mg of a medication by injection. the vial contains 40 mg/ml. how many ml should be given? (60 mg ÷ 40 mg) × 1 ml = 1.5 ml. check: the order is more than 40 mg, so you need more than 1 ml.

the safe dose range for a medication is 25–50 mg/kg/day. a child weighs 18 kg. the order is 250 mg every 8 hours. is the order within the safe range? yes. the child gets 750 mg/day, and the safe range is 450–900 mg/day. no. 750 mg/day is above the safe maximum. no. 250 mg is below the safe minimum of 450 mg. yes, because 250 mg is less than 18 × 50 = 900 mg. first find the safe daily range: 18 kg × 25 mg/kg = 450 mg/day and 18 kg × 50 mg/kg = 900 mg/day. every 8 hours means 3 doses a day (24 ÷ 8 = 3), so the child gets 250 mg × 3 = 750 mg/day. 750 mg/day is between 450 and 900, so the order is safe. compare daily to daily: one dose (250 mg) can't be compared with a per-day range.

an iv of 1,000 ml is ordered to run over 8 hours. at what rate should the pump be set, in ml per hour? 125 ml/h 8,000 ml/h 100 ml/h 80 ml/h ml per hour = total ml ÷ hours. 1,000 ml ÷ 8 h = 125 ml/h. 8,000 comes from multiplying instead of dividing.
a 500-ml iv bag is infusing at 100 ml per hour. how many hours will it take for the bag to finish? time = total volume ÷ rate. 500 ml ÷ 100 ml/h = 5 hours.

an iv of 1,500 ml is to run over 12 hours. the tubing's drop factor is 20 drops (gtt) per ml. what is the flow rate in drops per minute, rounded to the nearest whole drop? 42 gtt/min 125 gtt/min 2,500 gtt/min 21 gtt/min gtt/min = (total ml × drop factor) ÷ total minutes. 12 hours = 12 × 60 = 720 minutes. (1,500 ml × 20 gtt/ml) ÷ 720 min = 30,000 ÷ 720 ≈ 41.7, which rounds to 42 gtt/min. 125 is the rate in ml per hour (1,500 ÷ 12), not drops per minute.

a 250-ml iv bag contains 500 mg of a medication. the order is 20 mg per hour. at what rate, in ml per hour, should the pump be set? 10 ml/h 40 ml/h 0.1 ml/h 5 ml/h first find the concentration: 500 mg ÷ 250 ml = 2 mg per ml. then divide the hourly dose by the concentration: 20 mg/h ÷ 2 mg/ml = 10 ml/h. 40 comes from multiplying 20 × 2 instead of dividing.

on the map, 1 inch = 10 miles. the straight-line distance from fresno to merced measures 7.2 inches on the map. how many miles apart are the two cities in a straight line? set up the proportion: 1 in / 10 mi = 7.2 in / x mi. x = 7.2 × 10 = 72 miles.

a cook wants to make 10 servings of the chili instead of 4. how many cups of beans will she need? scale factor = 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5. beans: 3 cups × 2.5 = 7.5 cups. (or set up 3/4 = x/10, so 4x = 30 and x = 7.5.)

the provider orders 400 mg of amoxicillin. using the label, how many ml should the nurse give? the label's concentration is 250 mg in 5 ml. set up: 250 mg / 5 ml = 400 mg / x ml. cross-multiply: 250x = 2,000, so x = 8 ml. (or use d/h × q: 400 ÷ 250 × 5 = 8 ml.)

using the label, how many full 400-mg doses can be given from the 100-ml bottle? 8 10 12 13 each 400-mg dose is 8 ml (400 ÷ 250 × 5). 100 ml ÷ 8 ml per dose = 12.5, so the bottle holds 12 full doses (the last 4 ml is only half a dose). rounding 12.5 up to 13 would mean planning a dose that isn't in the bottle.

which box of gauze pads is the better buy, and what is its price per pad? brand a, $0.25 per pad brand b, $0.23 per pad brand b, $0.25 per pad brand a, $0.23 per pad unit price = total price ÷ number of pads. brand a: $6.25 ÷ 25 = $0.25 per pad. brand b: $9.20 ÷ 40 = $0.23 per pad. brand b costs less per pad, so it is the better buy even though the box costs more.
using the table, how many nurses must be on duty in a medical-surgical unit with 30 patients? medical-surgical ratio: 1 nurse for every 5 patients. 30 patients ÷ 5 = 6 nurses.
what is 20% of 85? 1,700 17 4.25 68 change the percent to a decimal: 20% = 0.20. 0.20 × 85 = 17. 4.25 divides 85 by 20, 68 is the other 80%, and 1,700 multiplies by 20 instead of 0.20.

a family's dinner bill at a fresno restaurant is $40.00. they leave a 15% tip. how many dollars is the tip? 15% = 0.15. 0.15 × 40 = 6, so the tip is $6.00. mental math: 10% of $40 is $4 and 5% is $2, so 15% is $4 + $2 = $6.

a pair of scrubs that normally costs $36 is on sale for 30% off. what is the sale price? $46.80 $25.20 $10.80 $6.00 discount = 30% of $36 = 0.30 × 36 = $10.80. sale price = $36 − $10.80 = $25.20. (or 70% of $36: 0.70 × 36 = $25.20.) $10.80 is only the discount. $6.00 subtracts 30 dollars, not 30%, and $46.80 adds the discount.

a stethoscope costs $120 before tax. the sales tax rate is 8.25%. what is the total cost with tax? $129.90 $219.00 $9.90 $128.25 tax = 8.25% of $120 = 0.0825 × 120 = $9.90. total = $120 + $9.90 = $129.90. $9.90 is only the tax. $128.25 adds 8.25 dollars, and $219.00 uses 0.825 instead of 0.0825.

a patient's weight dropped from 180 lb to 162 lb. what was the percent decrease? 18% 11.1% 90% 10% amount of change: 180 − 162 = 18 lb. percent change = change ÷ original × 100 = 18 ÷ 180 × 100 = 10%. 11.1% divides by the new weight (162). 18% is the pounds lost, not a percent, and 90% is the new weight as a percent of the old.
12 is what percent of 48? part ÷ whole = 12 ÷ 48 = 0.25. 0.25 × 100 = 25%.
30 is 40% of what number? 12 120 75 70 write the equation: 30 = 0.40 × n. divide: n = 30 ÷ 0.40 = 75. 12 is 40% of 30, which answers a different question. 120 multiplies 30 × 4, and 70 adds 30 + 40.

a store takes 20% off a $50 backpack, then takes an extra 10% off the sale price at the register. what is the final price? $14.00 $40.00 $36.00 $35.00 first discount: 80% of $50 = 0.80 × 50 = $40. second discount is 10% of the new price: 0.90 × 40 = $36. $35 adds the percents (30% off the original), which overstates the discount. $40 stops after one discount, and $14 is the total amount saved.

a blood pressure monitor costs $80. the price is raised 25%, and later the new price is lowered by 20%. what is the final price? $100.00 $80.00 $76.00 $84.00 increase: 1.25 × 80 = $100. decrease 20% of $100: 0.80 × 100 = $80. the price is back where it started. $84 comes from adding +25% and −20% to get a 5% increase. the 20% is taken from $100, not $80, so the two changes are not the same size in dollars.

a 1,000-ml iv bag is 35% infused. how many milliliters are left in the bag? 650 ml 35 ml 965 ml 350 ml 35% has gone in, so 100% − 35% = 65% is left. 0.65 × 1,000 = 650 ml. 350 ml is the amount already infused, and 965 ml subtracts 35 ml instead of 35%.
what is 0.5% of 400? 2 200 0.2 20 0.5% as a decimal is 0.005 (move the decimal two places left). 0.005 × 400 = 2. 200 treats 0.5% as 50%, and 20 treats it as 5%.

which are equal to 25% of 80? select all that apply. 20 0.25 × 80 80 × 25 80 ÷ 4 80 − 25 25% = 0.25 = 1/4, so 25% of 80 = 0.25 × 80 = 80 ÷ 4 = 20. 80 × 25 = 2,000 forgets to change the percent to a decimal. 80 − 25 = 55 subtracts the number 25 instead of taking 25%.
a medical-equipment salesperson earns a 6% commission. how many dollars of commission does she earn on a $2,350 sale? 6% = 0.06. 0.06 × 2,350 = 141, so the commission is $141.

a central valley town grew from 130,000 people to 143,000 people. what was the percent increase? 9.1% 13% 10% 110% change: 143,000 − 130,000 = 13,000. percent increase = 13,000 ÷ 130,000 × 100 = 10%. 9.1% divides by the new population. 13% treats 13,000 people as 13 percent, and 110% is the new population as a percent of the old one.

after a 30% discount, a textbook costs $63. what was the original price, in dollars? after 30% off, the sale price is 70% of the original: 0.70 × original = 63. original = 63 ÷ 0.70 = $90. a tempting mistake is 63 × 1.30 = $81.90. that adds 30% of the sale price, but the discount was 30% of the original.

a student answered 45 out of 60 practice questions correctly. what percent did she get correct? 133% 15% 45% 75% percent = part ÷ whole × 100 = 45 ÷ 60 × 100. 45 ÷ 60 = 0.75 = 75%. 45% treats the raw score as a percent, 15% is the number missed, and 133% divides 60 ÷ 45.

a provider lowers a patient's daily dose of a medication by 15%. the old dose was 400 mg. what is the new dose? decrease = 15% of 400 = 0.15 × 400 = 60 mg. new dose = 400 − 60 = 340 mg. (or 85% of 400: 0.85 × 400 = 340.)

ana puts $1,500 in a savings account that pays 4% simple interest per year. how much interest does she earn in 3 years? $60.00 $1,800.00 $1,680.00 $180.00 simple interest: i = principal × rate × time. i = 1,500 × 0.04 × 3 = $180. $60 is only one year of interest, $1,680 is the total balance (not the interest), and $1,800 uses 0.4 instead of 0.04.

of 240 students in a science course, 60% are pre-nursing majors. of the pre-nursing majors, 25% are first-generation college students. how many students are pre-nursing and first-generation? 60 36 144 96 pre-nursing: 0.60 × 240 = 144 students. first-generation pre-nursing: 0.25 × 144 = 36 students. 60 takes 25% of all 240 students, 144 stops after the first step, and 96 is the number of students who are not pre-nursing.

a pharmacy raises the price of a $50 item by 20%. which expressions give the new price? select all that apply. 50 × 1.2 50 + 0.2 × 50 50 × 0.2 50 + 20 50 + 10 20% of $50 is 0.2 × 50 = $10, so the new price is 50 + 10 = $60. 50 × 1.2 = $60 too, since 100% + 20% = 120% = 1.2. 50 × 0.2 gives only the $10 increase, and 50 + 20 adds 20 dollars instead of 20%.

a pair of nursing shoes costs $80. put these offers in order from the lowest final price to the highest final price. 25% off 30% off, then 10% sales tax $18 off 15% off, then $5 off 25% off: 0.75 × 80 = $60.00. 30% off then 10% tax: 0.70 × 80 = $56, and 1.10 × 56 = $61.60. $18 off: 80 − 18 = $62.00. 15% off then $5 off: 0.85 × 80 = $68, and 68 − 5 = $63.00.
a patient's weight dropped from 200 lb to 180 lb. what is the percent decrease? (type a number only.) change = 20 lb. percent change = 20 ÷ 200 (the original) × 100 = 10%.
scrubs cost $40 and are on sale for 30% off. what is the sale price? $12 $28 $37 $52 discount = 0.30 × 40 = $12. sale price = 40 − 12 = $28.
a $60 textbook has 8.25% sales tax. what is the total cost? $64.95 $68.25 $60.50 $65.50 tax = 0.0825 × 60 = $4.95. total = $64.95.
after a 20% raise, a cna earns $24 per hour. what was the hourly pay before the raise? (type a number.) new pay = 1.20 × old pay, so old pay = 24 ÷ 1.20 = $20.
a class had 40 students. 35% were nursing majors. how many students were not nursing majors? 14 26 35 5 nursing majors: 0.35 × 40 = 14. not nursing: 40 − 14 = 26.

d5w is a 5% dextrose solution, which means 5 g of dextrose in every 100 ml. how many grams of dextrose are in a 1,000-ml bag? 50 g 5 g 500 g 0.5 g 5% means 5 g per 100 ml. 1,000 ml is 10 times 100 ml, so it holds 10 × 5 g = 50 g. or use a proportion: 5/100 = x/1,000, so x = 50 g.

an adult's maximum daily dose of acetaminophen is 4 g. a patient has taken 2,600 mg today. what percent of the daily maximum has the patient taken? make the units match first: 4 g = 4,000 mg. percent = part ÷ whole × 100 = 2,600 ÷ 4,000 × 100 = 65%.
on the receipt, the sales tax is 8% of the subtotal. how much is the tax? 8% = 0.08. tax = 0.08 × $46.00 = $3.68.

a family pays the subtotal, the 8% tax, and an 18% tip calculated on the subtotal. about how much do they pay in all? $54.28 $57.96 $58.88 $49.68 tax: 0.08 × 46 = $3.68. tip: 0.18 × 46 = $8.28. total: 46.00 + 3.68 + 8.28 = $57.96. (shortcut: 46 × 1.26 = 57.96, because 8% + 18% = 26%.)

a student buys the stethoscope at the sale price and then gets the extra 10% off. what does she pay (before tax)? $48.00 $50.40 $52.00 $56.00 sale price: 30% off $80 → 80 × 0.70 = $56.00. extra 10% off the sale price: 56 × 0.90 = $50.40. trap: 30% + 10% is not 40% off. taking 40% off $80 would give $48.00, but the second discount is taken from the smaller sale price.
according to the label, 690 mg of sodium is 30% of the daily value. what is the full daily value for sodium, in mg? 30% of the daily value = 690 mg, so 0.30 × dv = 690. dv = 690 ÷ 0.30 = 2,300 mg.

using the table, what was the percent change in applicants from 2024 to 2025? 10% decrease 11.1% decrease 60% decrease 12.5% increase percent change = (new − old) ÷ old × 100. (540 − 600) ÷ 600 = −60 ÷ 600 = −0.10, a 10% decrease. trap: dividing by the new value (60 ÷ 540 ≈ 11.1%) gives the wrong answer. always divide by the starting (old) value.
solve for x: 3x + 7 = 22 29/3 3 5 15 subtract 7 from both sides: 3x = 15. divide both sides by 3: x = 5. 15 forgets to divide by 3. 29/3 adds 7 instead of subtracting it.

evaluate 2a² − 3b when a = 4 and b = −2. 26 38 22 70 substitute: 2(4)² − 3(−2). exponent first: 4² = 16, so 2 × 16 = 32. then −3 × −2 = +6. 32 + 6 = 38. 26 drops the negative sign on b (32 − 6). 70 squares 2 × 4 = 8 to get 64. 22 reads a² as a × 2.
solve for x: 5(x − 2) = 3x + 8 distribute: 5x − 10 = 3x + 8. subtract 3x from both sides: 2x − 10 = 8. add 10: 2x = 18, so x = 9. check: 5(9 − 2) = 35 and 3(9) + 8 = 35 ✓

which equation represents this sentence? "seven less than twice a number n is 15." 2n − 7 = 15 2(n − 7) = 15 2n + 7 = 15 7 − 2n = 15 "twice a number" is 2n. "seven less than" something means start with that thing and subtract 7: 2n − 7. 7 − 2n reverses the order. 2(n − 7) subtracts 7 before doubling.
solve the inequality: −4x + 6 > 18 x 3 x −3 subtract 6 from both sides: −4x > 12. divide both sides by −4. dividing by a negative flips the inequality sign: x −3 forgets to flip the sign.

simplify: 3(2y − 5) − 4y + 9 2y + 4 10y − 6 2y − 6 2y − 24 distribute: 6y − 15 − 4y + 9. combine like terms: 6y − 4y = 2y and −15 + 9 = −6. so the answer is 2y − 6. 2y + 4 forgets to multiply the −5 by 3, 10y − 6 adds 4y instead of subtracting it, and 2y − 24 subtracts the 9 instead of adding it.
solve for x: x/4 = 9 undo division by multiplying both sides by 4. x = 9 × 4 = 36.

a gym near fresno city college charges a $25 sign-up fee plus $15 per month. jamal has paid $130 in total. how many months has he been a member? 8.67 10.33 105 7 write the equation: 25 + 15m = 130. subtract the fee: 15m = 105. divide: m = 7 months. 8.67 forgets to subtract the sign-up fee, 10.33 adds the fee instead, and 105 stops before dividing by 15.

the formula f = (9/5)c + 32 changes celsius to fahrenheit. which formula correctly solves for c? c = (5/9)(f − 32) c = (5/9)f − 32 c = (9/5)(f − 32) c = (5/9)(f + 32) subtract 32 from both sides: f − 32 = (9/5)c. multiply both sides by 5/9 (the reciprocal of 9/5): c = (5/9)(f − 32). c = (5/9)f − 32 subtracts 32 in the wrong order. using 9/5 again does not undo the multiplication, and + 32 does not undo + 32.

which values of x make 2x − 1 ≤ 7 true? select all that apply. −2 0 4 4.5 6 add 1 to both sides: 2x ≤ 8. divide by 2: x ≤ 4. −2, 0, and 4 are all less than or equal to 4. (4 works because the sign includes "equal to.") 4.5 and 6 are greater than 4. check 4.5: 2(4.5) − 1 = 8, and 8 is not ≤ 7.

a dietitian tells a patient to eat at most 2,000 mg of sodium per day. which inequality shows this, where s is milligrams of sodium? s 2,000 s ≥ 2,000 s ≤ 2,000 "at most" means the amount can be 2,000 or anything less, so use ≤. s mean "at least" and "more than."

a school play sells adult tickets for $12 and child tickets for $8. a family group buys 15 tickets for $156. how many adult tickets did they buy? let a = adult tickets, so 15 − a = child tickets. 12a + 8(15 − a) = 156 → 12a + 120 − 8a = 156. 4a = 36, so a = 9 adult tickets (and 6 child tickets). check: 9 × $12 + 6 × $8 = $108 + $48 = $156 ✓
evaluate 4(n + 3) when n = 5. 20 32 23 12 parentheses first: 5 + 3 = 8. multiply: 4 × 8 = 32. 23 multiplies only the n (4 × 5 + 3), 12 adds everything, and 20 drops the 3.

a farm stand sells almonds for $6.50 per pound and charges $2 for a reusable bag. which equation gives the total cost c, in dollars, of p pounds of almonds in one bag? c = 2p + 6.50 c = 6.50p + 2 p = 6.50c + 2 c = 8.50p the price per pound multiplies the number of pounds: 6.50p. the $2 bag fee is charged once, so it is added: c = 6.50p + 2. c = 8.50p charges the bag fee on every pound. c = 2p + 6.50 swaps the rate and the fee.
solve for x: 0.4x + 1.2 = 3.6 subtract 1.2: 0.4x = 2.4. divide by 0.4: x = 2.4 ÷ 0.4 = 6.

which expression is equivalent to −3(4 − 2x)? −12 + 6x −12 − 2x −12 − 6x 12 + 6x multiply −3 by each term inside: −3 × 4 = −12 and −3 × (−2x) = +6x. so −3(4 − 2x) = −12 + 6x. −12 − 6x misses that a negative times a negative is positive. −12 − 2x only multiplies the first term.

the sum of three consecutive integers is 87. what is the largest of the three integers? 30 29 43 28 let the integers be n, n + 1, and n + 2. then 3n + 3 = 87. 3n = 84, so n = 28. the integers are 28, 29, and 30. the question asks for the largest, which is 30. 28 is the smallest and 29 is the middle one.

which expression is equivalent to 5x − 2(x + 4)? 7x − 8 3x − 4 3x − 8 3x + 8 distribute the −2: −2 × x = −2x and −2 × 4 = −8. 5x − 2x − 8 = 3x − 8. 3x + 8 loses the negative on the 8, 3x − 4 forgets to multiply the 4 by 2, and 7x − 8 adds 2x.

which expressions are equivalent to 2(x + 3)? select all that apply. 2x + 6 2x + 3 x + x + 6 6 + 2x 2x + 5 distribute: 2(x + 3) = 2x + 6. x + x + 6 is also 2x + 6, and 6 + 2x is the same sum in a different order. 2x + 3 forgets to multiply the 3 by 2. 2x + 5 adds 2 to the 3 instead of multiplying.

put the steps for solving 3x − 4 = 2x + 6 in the correct order. subtract 2x from both sides: x − 4 = 6 add 4 to both sides: x = 10 check: 3(10) − 4 = 26 and 2(10) + 6 = 26 get the variable on one side first by subtracting 2x. then undo the − 4 by adding 4, which gives x = 10. finally, plug x = 10 back in to check that both sides match.

maria has a $60 grocery budget and has already spent $18.50. apples cost $1.25 per pound. which is the greatest whole number of pounds of apples she can buy without going over budget? 48 14 34 33 write an inequality: 18.50 + 1.25p ≤ 60. 1.25p ≤ 41.50, so p ≤ 41.50 ÷ 1.25 = 33.2. she can buy at most 33 whole pounds. rounding up to 34 would cost 18.50 + 42.50 = $61, which is over budget. 48 ignores the $18.50 already spent, and 14 divides the $18.50 already spent by 1.25.

body mass index can be found with bmi = 703w ÷ h², where w is weight in pounds and h is height in inches. what is the bmi of a person who weighs 150 lb and is 65 inches tall? round to the nearest tenth. 0.04 811.2 1,622.3 25.0 square the height first: 65² = 65 × 65 = 4,225. 703 × 150 = 105,450. 105,450 ÷ 4,225 ≈ 24.96, which rounds to 25.0. 1,622.3 forgets to square the height, 811.2 doubles it (65 × 2) instead of squaring, and 0.04 forgets the 703.

a nursing program in visalia requires a teas score of at least 65%. which inequality shows the scores s that meet the requirement? s ≥ 65 s > 65 s ≤ 65 s < 65 "at least 65" means 65 or anything higher, so 65 itself counts. greater than or equal to: s ≥ 65.

a patient on a fluid restriction may drink no more than 1,500 ml per day. she has already had 3 cups of water, each 240 ml. which inequality shows how many more milliliters, x, she may drink today? 720 + x ≥ 1,500 3x + 240 ≤ 1,500 720 + x ≤ 1,500 720 + x < 1,500 she has already had 3 × 240 = 720 ml, so her total for the day is 720 + x. "no more than 1,500" means 1,500 or less, so use ≤: 720 + x ≤ 1,500.
solve for x: 3x − 7 = 20 add 7: 3x = 27. divide by 3: x = 9.
simplify: 4(x + 3) − 2x 2x + 3 2x + 12 6x + 12 2x + 7 distribute: 4x + 12. combine like terms: 4x − 2x = 2x. answer: 2x + 12.
solve: 2x + 5 > 17 x > 6 x 11 x > 22 subtract 5: 2x > 12. divide by 2: x > 6. (dividing by a positive number doesn't flip the sign.)
evaluate 2a² − b when a = 3 and b = 4. a² = 9. 2 × 9 = 18. 18 − 4 = 14.
which expression represents "5 less than twice a number n"? 5 − 2n 2n − 5 2(n − 5) 2 + n − 5 "twice a number" is 2n. "5 less than" means subtract 5 from it: 2n − 5.
solve for x: −3x + 4 ≤ 19 x ≤ −5 x ≥ −5 x ≥ 5 x ≤ 5 subtract 4: −3x ≤ 15. divide by −3 and flip the sign: x ≥ −5.
solve for x: (x/4) + 3 = 10 subtract 3: x/4 = 7. multiply by 4: x = 28.
which is a like term to 7xy? 7x −3xy 7y xy² like terms have the same variables with the same exponents: −3xy matches xy.

a medication order is for d milligrams. the medication on hand contains h milligrams in q milliliters. which expression gives the number of milliliters to give? (d ÷ h) × q (h ÷ d) × q d × h × q (d × h) ÷ q divide what you want (d) by what you have (h) to find how many 'portions' you need. each portion is q ml, so multiply by q: ml = (d ÷ h) × q. check with numbers: if d = 500 mg and the bottle has h = 250 mg in q = 5 ml, then (500 ÷ 250) × 5 = 10 ml.

a home-care agency in modesto uses the equation c = 45h + 20 to find the total cost c, in dollars, of h hours of care. which statement is true? c is the independent variable, and h is the dependent variable. 20 is the independent variable, and c is the dependent variable. both h and c are dependent variables. h is the independent variable, and c is the dependent variable. the family chooses how many hours of care to buy, so h is the input: the independent variable. the cost depends on the hours, so c is the output: the dependent variable.
which inequality is graphed on the number line? x ≥ −2 x > −2 x −2.

a patient may take no more than 3 tablets per day. which inequality matches the graph? x 3 x ≤ 3 x ≥ 3 "no more than 3" means 3 or fewer. the circle at 3 is filled (3 is allowed) and the shading goes left: x ≤ 3.

solve 3x − 4 ≥ 11. then click the number line that shows the solution. add 4 to both sides: 3x ≥ 15. divide by 3: x ≥ 5. ≥ means 5 is included (filled circle) and the shading goes right toward bigger numbers. that's graph c. b has an open circle (x > 5), a shades the wrong way (x ≤ 5), and d starts at −5.

solve −2x + 3 > 9. then click the number line that shows the solution. subtract 3 from both sides: −2x > 6. divide both sides by −2. dividing by a negative flips the inequality sign: x < −3. x < −3 is an open circle at −3 with shading to the left: graph a. graph b is the answer you get if you forget to flip the sign.

a safe range for a lab value is graphed below. which inequality describes the graph? −1 4 the shading is between −1 and 4, so x is between them. the circle at −1 is filled (−1 included: ≤), and the circle at 4 is open (4 not included: <). so −1 ≤ x < 4.
a clinic's small waiting room must hold fewer than 12 people, written p p says the same thing as p < 12, read from the other side.

a certified nursing assistant earns $18 per hour. this week she wants to earn more than $450, but she can work no more than 30 hours. which pair of inequalities describes the number of hours, h, she can work? 18h ≥ 450 and h 450 and h ≥ 30 h + 18 > 450 and h ≤ 30 18h > 450 and h ≤ 30 pay is $18 for each hour, so earnings are 18h. "more than $450" means 18h > 450. "no more than 30 hours" means 30 or fewer: h ≤ 30.

which is the best estimate of 48.7 × 2.1? 1,000 51 100 50 round each number: 48.7 ≈ 50 and 2.1 ≈ 2. 50 × 2 = 100. (the exact answer is 102.27.) 50 forgets to multiply by 2, 51 adds instead of multiplying (48.7 + 2.1 ≈ 51), and 1,000 is off by a factor of 10.

at a grocery store in merced, lupe buys items costing $3.89, $6.12, $11.95, and $2.49. rounding each price to the nearest dollar, what is the best estimate of the total? $20 $24 $26 $22 round each price: $3.89 → $4, $6.12 → $6, $11.95 → $12, $2.49 → $2. add: 4 + 6 + 12 + 2 = $24. (the exact total is $24.45.) $22 drops the cents instead of rounding (3 + 6 + 11 + 2), $26 rounds every price up, and $20 rounds to the nearest $5 instead of the nearest $1.
a nurse works three 12-hour shifts each week. how many hours does she work in 4 weeks? hours per week: 3 × 12 = 36. hours in 4 weeks: 36 × 4 = 144.

diego drives from fresno to visalia and back for clinicals 5 days a week. it is 44 miles each way. his car gets 30 miles per gallon, and gas costs $4.80 per gallon. how much does he spend on gas each week? $70.40 $14.08 $140.80 $35.20 miles per week: 44 × 2 trips × 5 days = 440 miles. gallons: 440 ÷ 30 ≈ 14.667 gallons. cost: 440 ÷ 30 × 4.80 = $70.40. $35.20 counts only one way each day, $14.08 is the cost for one day, and $140.80 counts four trips a day.

a patient takes 1 tablet 3 times a day for 14 days. how many tablets are needed? 42 17 14 28 tablets per day: 1 × 3 = 3. tablets for 14 days: 3 × 14 = 42. 17 adds 3 + 14, and 28 uses 2 tablets per day.

a pre-nursing club sells bags of almonds for $8 each to raise $500 for teas prep books. they have sold 47 bags so far. how many more bags must they sell to reach at least $500? 453 16 63 15 bags needed in all: 500 ÷ 8 = 62.5, so they must sell 63 bags (62 bags would only raise $496). more bags: 63 − 47 = 16. 15 rounds 62.5 − 47 = 15.5 down, which leaves them $4 short. 63 is the total, not the number still needed, and 453 subtracts bags from dollars.

a patient needs 3.2 l of iv fluid over the next day. the fluid comes in 250-ml bags. what is the fewest number of full bags that must be hung? convert: 3.2 l = 3,200 ml. 3,200 ÷ 250 = 12.8 bags. 12 bags would give only 3,000 ml, so round up to 13 bags.
which is the best estimate of 19% of 402? 800 80 8 40 round: 19% ≈ 20% and 402 ≈ 400. 20% of 400 = 0.20 × 400 = 80. (the exact value is 76.38.) 8 and 800 misplace the decimal point, and 40 uses 10%.

on a trip from bakersfield to merced, a driver goes 55 mph for 2 hours and then 70 mph for 1.5 hours. what total distance does the driver cover? 218.8 miles 215 miles 125 miles 245 miles distance = rate × time for each part. part 1: 55 × 2 = 110 miles. part 2: 70 × 1.5 = 105 miles. total: 110 + 105 = 215 miles. 218.8 averages the two speeds, which does not work because the times are different. 125 adds the speeds, and 245 uses 70 mph for the whole 3.5 hours.

rosa buys 3 shirts for $14 each and 2 pairs of pants for $22 each. which expressions give her total cost? select all that apply. 3(14) + 2(22) 42 + 44 5(14 + 22) 3 + 14 + 2 + 22 2(22) + 3(14) shirts cost 3 × 14 = $42 and pants cost 2 × 22 = $44, for $86 total. 3(14) + 2(22), 42 + 44, and 2(22) + 3(14) all equal 86. 5(14 + 22) = $180 charges every item for both a shirt and pants, and 3 + 14 + 2 + 22 adds the counts to the prices.
kai pays for a $13.65 lunch with a $20 bill. how many dollars in change should he get? change = amount paid − cost. $20.00 − $13.65 = $6.35.

one serving of trail mix has 140 calories. a student eats 1.5 servings. how many calories does she eat? 280 93.3 141.5 210 multiply the calories per serving by the number of servings. 140 × 1.5 = 210 calories. 280 uses 2 servings, 141.5 adds 1.5, and 93.3 divides 140 by 1.5.

a certified nursing assistant earns $22 per hour for the first 40 hours in a week and 1.5 times that rate for each hour over 40. how much does she earn for a 46-hour week? $1,012.00 $1,518.00 $946.00 $1,078.00 regular pay: 40 × $22 = $880. overtime rate: 1.5 × $22 = $33. overtime pay: 6 × $33 = $198. total: $880 + $198 = $1,078. $1,012 pays all 46 hours at $22, $1,518 pays all 46 hours at $33, and $946 pays only the extra $11 for the overtime hours.

a community clinic sees about 237 patients per week. which is the best estimate of how many patients it sees in a year? 2,400 1,200 12,000 120,000 a year has about 52 weeks; round to 50 weeks and 237 to 240. 240 × 50 = 12,000. (the exact value is 237 × 52 = 12,324.) 1,200 and 120,000 are off by a factor of 10, and 2,400 uses only 10 weeks.
four roommates in clovis split the rent of $2,140 and the utility bill of $196 equally. how many dollars does each roommate pay? total cost: $2,140 + $196 = $2,336. each person: $2,336 ÷ 4 = $584.

a 72-acre farm near kerman plants 1/2 of its land in almonds and 1/6 in pistachios. the rest is planted in grapes. how many acres are planted in grapes? 12 36 24 48 almonds: 1/2 × 72 = 36 acres. pistachios: 1/6 × 72 = 12 acres. grapes: 72 − 36 − 12 = 24 acres. 48 is the acres planted in almonds and pistachios together. 12 is the pistachios and 36 is the almonds.
which is the best estimate of 397 + 512? 800 90 1,000 900 round to the nearest hundred: 397 ≈ 400 and 512 ≈ 500. 400 + 500 = 900. (the exact sum is 909.)

a nurse completes 3 patient charts every 40 minutes. at this rate, how many charts can she fully complete in 6.5 hours? 29 26 48 30 change hours to minutes: 6.5 × 60 = 390 minutes. number of 40-minute blocks: 390 ÷ 40 = 9.75. charts: 9.75 × 3 = 29.25, so she can fully complete 29 charts. 30 rounds up to a chart she has not finished. 26 uses 6.5 × 4. 48 treats 6.5 hours as 650 minutes.

a student has $1,200 saved for the semester. tuition is $46 per unit for 12 units, and books cost $310. how much money will she have left? $338.00 $844.00 $648.00 $890.00 tuition: $46 × 12 = $552. total spent: $552 + $310 = $862. left: $1,200 − $862 = $338. $648 forgets the books, $890 forgets the tuition, and $844 charges tuition for only 1 unit.

which is the best estimate of 4 7/8 × 3 1/9? 20 8 12 15 round each mixed number to the nearest whole number: 4 7/8 ≈ 5 and 3 1/9 ≈ 3. 5 × 3 = 15. (the exact product is about 15.2.) 12 rounds 4 7/8 down to 4, 20 rounds 3 1/9 up to 4, and 8 adds instead of multiplying.

a patient's goal is to drink at least 2,000 ml of fluid today. use 1 cup = 240 ml. which of these would meet the goal? select all that apply. one 2-l bottle four 500-ml bottles 1.5 l plus 3 cups 8 cups 1 l plus three 300-ml cartons one 2-l bottle = 2,000 ml and four 500-ml bottles = 2,000 ml. both meet "at least 2,000." 1.5 l + 3 cups = 1,500 + 720 = 2,220 ml, which meets the goal. 8 cups = 8 × 240 = 1,920 ml, and 1 l + 3 × 300 ml = 1,900 ml. both fall short.

put these trips in order from the shortest travel time to the longest travel time. 45 miles at 30 mph 100 miles at 50 mph 135 miles at 60 mph 160 miles at 64 mph time = distance ÷ speed. 45 ÷ 30 = 1.5 h; 100 ÷ 50 = 2 h; 135 ÷ 60 = 2.25 h; 160 ÷ 64 = 2.5 h. the longest trip in miles is not automatically the one with the longest time; you must divide by the speed.
a student studies 45 minutes each day for 12 days. about how many hours is that in total? 5 9 12 45 45 × 12 = 540 minutes. 540 ÷ 60 = 9 hours.

a nurse works three 12-hour shifts each week at $38 per hour. how much does she earn in 4 weeks before taxes? (type a number.) hours per week: 3 × 12 = 36. hours in 4 weeks: 144. pay: 144 × $38 = $5,472.
ana has $500. she spends $135 on books and $48 on a lab kit. then she earns $90. how much does she have now? $317 $407 $227 $773 500 − 135 − 48 + 90 = 407.
a box of 100 gloves costs $8. a clinic uses 650 gloves a week. how much does it spend on gloves each week? $52 $65 $48 $80 650 gloves = 6.5 boxes. 6.5 × $8 = $52.

two nurses split 54 patient assessments so that one does twice as many as the other. how many does the busier nurse do? 18 27 36 40 let x = the smaller share; 2x + x = 54 → x = 18. the busier nurse does 2 × 18 = 36.
a pharmacy fills 340 prescriptions on monday, which is 85% of its daily goal. what is the daily goal? 340 = 0.85 × goal → goal = 340 ÷ 0.85 = 400.
which is the best estimate of 29% of 61? 6 18 30 42 about 30% of 60 = 18.

a patient is told to take 2 tablets twice a day for 3 days, then 1 tablet twice a day for 4 days. how many tablets should the pharmacy dispense? 20 tablets 16 tablets 12 tablets 28 tablets first part: 2 tablets × 2 times/day × 3 days = 12 tablets. second part: 1 tablet × 2 times/day × 4 days = 8 tablets. total: 12 + 8 = 20 tablets.
an iv is infusing at 75 ml per hour. it was started at 0700. how many milliliters will have infused by 1300? from 0700 to 1300 is 13 − 7 = 6 hours. 6 h × 75 ml/h = 450 ml.

a child's dose is ordered in mg/kg, the child's weight is given in pounds, and the medication is a liquid labeled in mg/ml. put the steps in order, first to last. convert the weight from pounds to kilograms (÷ 2.2). multiply kilograms by the mg/kg order to get the dose in mg. divide the dose in mg by the concentration (mg/ml) to get ml. check that the answer is reasonable before giving it. the order is per kilogram, so weight must be in kg first. kg × mg/kg = mg, the dose the child needs. mg ÷ (mg/ml) = ml, the volume to measure. last, ask whether the number makes sense (kilograms should be smaller than pounds; a child's dose should not fill a whole cup).

using the pay stub, what is the cna's gross pay for the week? (overtime pays 1.5 times the regular rate.) regular pay: 40 × $19.50 = $780.00. overtime rate: 1.5 × 19.50 = $29.25 per hour. overtime pay: 6 × 29.25 = $175.50. gross pay: 780.00 + 175.50 = $955.50.

a student uses about 8 gb of data a month. which plan costs the least for her, and how much is it? basic, $85 plus, $55 unlimited, $65 plus, $40 basic: $25 + (8 − 2) × $10 = 25 + 60 = $85. plus: $40 + (8 − 5) × $5 = 40 + 15 = $55. unlimited: $65. the cheapest is plus at $55.

a student must be in her lab at fresno city college by 8:00 a.m. it takes 15 minutes to walk from the college bus stop to the lab. what is the latest bus she can catch at shaw & blackstone? 6:42 a.m. 7:12 a.m. 7:42 a.m. 7:25 a.m. work backward: she must reach the college stop by 8:00 − 15 min = 7:45 a.m. bus 2 reaches the college at 7:49, which is 4 minutes too late (she'd get to the lab at 8:04). bus 1 reaches the college at 7:19. so she must take bus 1, which leaves shaw & blackstone at 6:42 a.m.

after paying all the listed expenses, the student puts 40% of what is left into savings. how much does she save each month? expenses: 575 + 320 + 210 + 55 = $1,160. left over: 1,450 − 1,160 = $290. savings: 0.40 × 290 = $116.

how many milligrams are in 2.5 grams? 2,500 mg 25,000 mg 250 mg 0.0025 mg 1 g = 1,000 mg, so multiply by 1,000. 2.5 × 1,000 = 2,500 mg. 0.0025 divides instead of multiplying. 250 and 25,000 move the decimal the wrong number of places.
convert 750 ml to liters. 1 l = 1,000 ml, so divide by 1,000. 750 ÷ 1,000 = 0.75 l.

a patient weighs 154 lb. what is the patient's weight in kilograms? (1 kg = 2.2 lb) 338.8 kg 70 kg 156.2 kg 151.8 kg pounds are the smaller unit, so the number of kilograms will be smaller: divide by 2.2. 154 ÷ 2.2 = 70 kg. 338.8 multiplies by 2.2 (the wrong direction). 151.8 and 156.2 subtract or add 2.2.

a child weighs 44 lb. the order is 15 mg per kg of body weight. how many milligrams should the child receive? (1 kg = 2.2 lb) convert weight: 44 ÷ 2.2 = 20 kg. dose: 15 mg/kg × 20 kg = 300 mg. a common error is 15 × 44 = 660 mg, which uses pounds instead of kilograms and would double the dose.

a medication is given at 7:45 p.m. how is this time written in military (24-hour) time? 0745 1745 1945 2045 for p.m. times after 12:59, add 12 to the hour: 7 + 12 = 19. 7:45 p.m. = 1945. 0745 is 7:45 a.m., 1745 is 5:45 p.m., and 2045 is 8:45 p.m.

a child has a temperature of 38.5°c. what is this in degrees fahrenheit? use °f = (9/5)°c + 32. 101.3°f 126.9°f 69.3°f 3.6°f multiply by 9/5 (or 1.8): 38.5 × 1.8 = 69.3. add 32: 69.3 + 32 = 101.3°f. 69.3 forgets to add 32. 3.6 uses the °f → °c formula, and 126.9 adds 32 before multiplying.

an iv of 1,000 ml is to run over 8 hours. the tubing's drop factor is 15 drops (gtt) per ml. what is the flow rate in drops per minute, to the nearest whole number? 31 gtt/min 1,875 gtt/min 125 gtt/min 2 gtt/min change hours to minutes: 8 × 60 = 480 minutes. gtt/min = (volume × drop factor) ÷ minutes = (1,000 × 15) ÷ 480 = 15,000 ÷ 480 = 31.25. round to 31 gtt/min. 125 is the rate in ml per hour, not drops per minute. 2 forgets the drop factor, and 1,875 divides by hours instead of minutes.

a dose of cough syrup is 10 ml. how many teaspoons is this? (1 tsp = 5 ml) 0.67 tsp 2 tsp 0.5 tsp 50 tsp divide by the number of ml in one teaspoon: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 tsp. 0.5 divides 5 by 10, 50 multiplies, and 0.67 uses 15 ml (that is a tablespoon, not a teaspoon).

a patient is 5 feet 4 inches tall. what is this height in centimeters, to the nearest tenth?
