researchers gave one group of nursing students a 20-minute nap before a skills test and asked another group to read quietly for 20 minutes. the napping group made fewer medication-calculation errors than the reading group. when the study was repeated with a 60-minute nap, the nappers did no better than the readers and said they felt groggy. which conclusion is best supported by the passage? napping always improves performance on skills tests. quiet reading is the best way to prepare for a skills test. a short nap may help test performance more than a long nap does. most nursing students do not get enough sleep at night. the 20-minute nap helped, but the 60-minute nap did not, so nap length seems to matter. "always" is too strong, since the long nap did not help. the study never shows reading to be best, and it says nothing about students' nighttime sleep.

signs of heat exhaustion include heavy sweating, cool and clammy skin, a fast but weak pulse, nausea, and muscle cramps. heat stroke is more serious: body temperature rises above 103 °f, the skin may become hot and dry, and the person may become confused or pass out. heat stroke is a medical emergency, so call 911 right away. according to the passage, which sign points to heat stroke rather than heat exhaustion? confusion along with hot, dry skin heavy sweating and a fast, weak pulse cool, clammy skin with nausea muscle cramps after working outside the passage lists hot, dry skin and confusion under heat stroke. heavy sweating, clammy skin, and cramps are listed as signs of heat exhaustion.

a sign on the refrigerator in the hospital break room reads: "please label all food with your name and the date. unlabeled items will be thrown out every friday at 3 p.m." what can most reasonably be inferred from the sign? the break-room refrigerator is not working properly. employees are not allowed to eat in the break room. unlabeled food has been left in the refrigerator in the past. food may be stored in the refrigerator only on fridays. a rule like this is usually posted because old, unlabeled food has been a problem. the sign assumes people store food there, so eating is allowed and the refrigerator works. friday is only the clean-out day.

about 30 percent of california's water supply comes from the sierra nevada snowpack. snow builds up in the mountains during winter and melts slowly in spring and summer, filling rivers and reservoirs. in warm years, more precipitation falls as rain instead of snow, so water runs off early, before farms and cities need it most. according to the passage, what happens in warm years? the snowpack melts more slowly than usual. more snow builds up in the mountains. reservoirs stay empty for the whole year, even in winter. more precipitation falls as rain and runs off early. the last sentence says that in warm years more precipitation falls as rain, so water runs off early. the other choices contradict the passage or go beyond it; it never says reservoirs stay empty.

when the charge nurse posted the holiday schedule, dev scanned it, sighed, and crossed his name off the sign-up sheet for the new year's eve potluck. then he texted his sister: "looks like we'll have to celebrate on the 2nd." what can most reasonably be inferred about dev? he does not get along with his sister. he is scheduled to work over the new year's holiday. he forgot to sign up for the potluck. he thinks the charge nurse made a mistake on the schedule. after reading the schedule, dev drops out of the potluck and moves his family celebration to january 2, which suggests he has to work. he had already signed up for the potluck, he is making plans with his sister, and nothing suggests he thinks the schedule is wrong.

community health workers, sometimes called promotores in spanish-speaking communities, help connect their neighbors with health care. they often live in the same neighborhoods they serve and speak the same languages. they may help families sign up for insurance, remind patients about appointments, or teach classes on managing diabetes. which statements are supported by the passage? select all that apply. community health workers often speak the same languages as the people they serve. community health workers may help families enroll in health insurance. community health workers prescribe diabetes medicine. community health workers may teach classes about managing diabetes. community health workers must hold a nursing license. the passage directly states that they share languages with their neighbors, help with insurance sign-ups, and teach diabetes classes. it says they teach about diabetes, not prescribe medicine, and it never mentions a nursing license.

last year, the merced food bank's mobile pantry visited five rural towns once a month. this year, after receiving a grant to buy a second truck, it visits ten towns twice a month. which conclusion is best supported by the passage? the food bank stopped delivering food to the larger cities. the grant let the food bank reach more towns more often. rural towns need less food than cities do. the food bank's first truck broke down and had to be replaced. after the grant paid for a second truck, the pantry went from 5 towns monthly to 10 towns twice a month. cities, comparisons of need, and a broken truck are never mentioned.

nurse practitioners (nps) are registered nurses who have completed graduate education. in california, nps can examine patients, order tests, and prescribe medicine. a recent change in state law allows some experienced nps to practice without a physician's supervision once they meet certain requirements. supporters hope the change will bring more care to rural areas, where doctors are scarce. based on the passage, which statement is most likely true? all registered nurses are allowed to prescribe medicine. nps no longer need a nursing license to practice. some rural areas do not have enough doctors. most physicians opposed the change in the law. the passage says doctors are "scarce" in rural areas, which means there are not enough of them. only nps, who have graduate education, can prescribe, not all rns; nps are registered nurses; physicians' opinions are never mentioned.

to reduce mosquitoes around your home, empty standing water from flowerpots, buckets, and old tires at least once a week. mosquitoes lay their eggs in water, and the eggs can become biting adults in about a week. wear insect repellent at dawn and dusk, when the mosquitoes that carry west nile virus are most active. according to the passage, why should standing water be emptied at least once a week? mosquito eggs can become biting adults in about a week. standing water attracts birds that carry west nile virus. old water can damage flowerpots and buckets. mosquitoes are most active at dawn and dusk. emptying water weekly removes eggs before they can grow into adults in "about a week." dawn and dusk explains when to wear repellent, not why to empty water. birds and damaged pots are not mentioned.

kai read the label on his new prescription bottle twice, then called the pharmacy. "the label says to take one tablet three times a day," he said, "but my doctor told me to take it once a day." what can most reasonably be inferred from the passage? kai forgot to take his medicine that morning. kai is unable to read the prescription label. the pharmacy is closed for the day. kai thinks there may be a mistake on the label. kai points out that the label does not match his doctor's instructions, so he suspects an error. he clearly read the label (he quotes it), he reached the pharmacy by phone, and nothing mentions a missed dose.

a clinic's flu vaccine shipment arrived in september. by mid-october, the clinic posted a sign: "flu shots now available only for adults 65 and older and patients with chronic health conditions. all others, please check back in november." which conclusion is best supported by the sign? flu vaccines do not work well for adults who are younger than 65. the clinic has stopped giving flu shots for the rest of the season. most of the clinic's patients are over 65 or have a chronic condition. the clinic has a limited supply, so higher-risk patients get shots first. limiting shots to higher-risk groups and asking others to return later suggests a short supply. the sign says others can come back in november, so shots have not stopped. nothing says the vaccine fails in younger adults or describes patient ages.

in a survey of 400 students at a community college, 62 percent said they worked more than 20 hours a week. students who worked more than 20 hours reported sleeping an average of 6.1 hours a night, compared with 7.2 hours for students who worked less. both groups said that lack of time was their biggest barrier to studying. which conclusion is not supported by the passage? working more than 20 hours a week causes students to earn lower grades. most of the students surveyed worked more than 20 hours a week. students who worked more hours reported less sleep on average. students in both groups felt they did not have enough time to study. the survey never measured grades, so a conclusion about grades is not supported. 62 percent is more than half, the sleep averages (6.1 vs 7.2 hours) are given, and both groups named lack of time as a barrier.

before donating blood, donors should eat a healthy meal and drink extra fluids. they must weigh at least 110 pounds and bring a photo id. after donating, they should avoid heavy lifting for the rest of the day. according to the passage, what should a donor avoid after donating blood? eating a meal drinking fluids heavy lifting showing a photo id the last sentence says to avoid heavy lifting for the rest of the day. eating, drinking fluids, and bringing id are things donors are told to do before donating.

i've lived on olive avenue for thirty years, and for most of them i watched the corner lot sit empty and full of weeds. last spring, a few neighbors and i cleared it out and planted tomatoes, chiles, and squash. this fall we gave away more than 200 pounds of vegetables to families on our street. what can most reasonably be inferred about the writer? the writer plans to move away from olive avenue. the writer is proud of the neighborhood garden project. the writer owns the corner lot. the writer sells vegetables at a farmers' market. the writer describes turning a weedy lot into a garden and giving away 200 pounds of food, details that show pride. nothing suggests moving or owning the lot, and the vegetables were given away, not sold.

click the sentence that best supports the idea that mr. ruiz was dehydrated. a dry mouth and dark urine are two signs that the body is low on water. working outside all afternoon could lead to dehydration, but it doesn't show that he actually was dehydrated. lunch and the hat don't point to dehydration.

the library extends its hours during finals week. from december 8 to december 15, it will open at 7 a.m. and close at midnight. laptops may be checked out for four hours at a time with a student id. according to the paragraph, how long can a student keep a laptop? until midnight four hours seventeen hours all of finals week the paragraph says "laptops may be checked out for four hours at a time." the other numbers describe library hours, not laptops.

marcus glanced at the clock for the third time, then back at the door. when the instructor finally walked in with a stack of graded exams, he wiped his palms on his jeans and sat up straight. what can the reader infer about marcus? he is impatient for class to end so he can leave. he is confident that he earned a high score. he is anxious about his exam grade. he is upset that the instructor arrived late. checking the clock, wiping sweaty palms, and sitting up when the graded exams arrive all point to nervousness about his grade.

the clinic's new phone system lets patients press 1 to refill a prescription, 2 to schedule an appointment, or 3 to speak with a nurse. patients who stay on the line are connected to the front desk. calls after 5 p.m. go to the answering service. a patient calls at 3 p.m. and stays on the line. who will answer? a nurse the pharmacy the front desk the answering service patients who stay on the line are connected to the front desk. 3 p.m. is before the 5 p.m. cutoff.

when the power went out at the nursing home, the generator started within ten seconds. residents on oxygen concentrators were moved to the dining room, where the backup outlets were marked in red. staff checked on every resident within thirty minutes. which inference is best supported? not every outlet in the building was on generator power. the generator powered every outlet in the building. the power outage lasted more than thirty minutes. most of the home's residents rely on oxygen concentrators. residents on oxygen were moved to the dining room, where backup outlets were marked in red. moving them only makes sense if other outlets lacked generator power.

according to the passage, what do bridge programs allow lvns to do? skip the rn licensing exam and start working sooner become nurse practitioners without going to graduate school qualify to become rns in less time than starting over work as cnas while they are in school paragraph 3 says bridge programs let lvns earn an associate degree and qualify for the rn exam "in less time than starting from scratch." they still take the licensing exam, and nurse practitioner programs are graduate programs mentioned later.

why did mai most likely hurry into room 9? mrs. okafor could fall if she walked alone. mrs. okafor was having trouble breathing. mai was late giving mrs. okafor her medicine. mrs. okafor had asked to call her family. mrs. okafor was climbing out of bed even though her wristband marked her as a fall risk. her breathing is mentioned only as slowing when she fell asleep, and no medicine or phone call is mentioned.

based on the passage, which person has a higher risk of severe valley fever? a 65-year-old man with diabetes a healthy 30-year-old who works in an office a teenager who recently had a cold a person who lives with someone who has valley fever the passage lists adults over 60 and people with diabetes as being at higher risk of severe disease; this man is both. living with an infected person does not matter because valley fever does not spread from person to person.

based on the passage, what would most likely happen during a long drought with no limits on pumping? surface water deliveries would increase. farmers would stop using their wells. groundwater levels would keep dropping. the land surface would rise. in dry years farmers pump more groundwater, and when more is pumped than refills, aquifer levels drop. deliveries are cut in dry years, wells are used more, and the land sinks rather than rises.

according to the passage, when does most deep sleep occur? toward morning early in the night during rem sleep only after seven hours of sleep paragraph 1 says "deep sleep is concentrated early in the night." rem periods, not deep sleep, grow longer toward morning, and rem is a separate stage from deep sleep.

a student in a clinical rotation gets a flu shot at the clinic on october 22. what does the student need to do to meet the october 31 deadline? upload proof of vaccination before october 24th bring a copy of the record to room 104 nothing more; the record will be uploaded for them fill out and submit the medical exemption form students who get the shot at the clinic "will have their records uploaded for them within two business days," which is well before october 31.

which student is most likely to be turned away without a shot? a student who signed up online for 2:45 p.m. on october 21 a student who walks in at 10:00 a.m. when every slot is filled a student who signed up for a time slot and brings a student id a student who arrives at room 104 on october 22 at 9:00 a.m. with a reservation walk-ins are accepted only if open slots remain at the end of each day. a walk-in when every slot is filled has no place.

based on the memo, which inference is best supported? the clinic will charge students who walk in without a time slot. last year's clinic in the student center had a long or crowded waiting line. most health sciences students cannot get the vaccine for medical reasons. the health sciences office will give the vaccine to students in their homes. the memo says the changes come from "high demand last year" and that the new room has "more space for a waiting line." both suggest last year's line was crowded.

which signs does the passage say mean the person needs medical care right away? select all that apply. cannot keep fluids down blood in the stool has not urinated in 8 hours is thirsty after drinking the solution is very sleepy or hard to wake the final sentence lists four warning signs: can't keep fluids down, blood in the stool, very sleepy or hard to wake, and no urine in 8 hours. thirst alone is not on the list.

a crew of 12 workers works a 5-hour shift. according to the rule in the passage, at least how much drinking water must the employer provide? 5 quarts 12 quarts 17 quarts 60 quarts one quart per worker per hour: 12 workers × 5 hours × 1 quart = 60 quarts (15 gallons).

according to the passage, why does a person get sick the first time a germ enters the body? the immune system ignores new germs completely until a vaccine is given. its defense takes one to two weeks to build, and the germ multiplies meanwhile. memory cells mistake the germ for the body's own cells and attack them instead. antibodies cannot be made until the person receives a booster dose. "immune cells need one to two weeks to recognize it and build a strong defense. during that delay, the virus multiplies and the person becomes sick."

based on the passage, what is the most likely reason a booster dose works quickly? it contains a stronger form of the germ than the first dose. memory cells from the first dose recognize it and respond fast. it replaces all of the body's antibodies with new ones. it prevents side effects from the first dose. the passage explains that memory cells "launch a fast, powerful response" to a germ they have seen before. a booster brings back material the memory cells already recognize.

why does the posting most likely list language fluency as "preferred"? every applicant must pass a language test before being hired. some residents may speak them, so it helps but isn't required. cnas must translate for doctors and nurses during every shift. the facility hires only staff who grew up speaking these languages. "preferred" items are helpful but not required. listing specific languages suggests that residents or families speak them.

how does marisol most likely feel at the beginning of the story? bored nervous angry confident she holds her clipboard "like a shield" and rereads the same line three times. both details show nervousness.

which detail helps marisol decide to speak spanish? mrs. ortega's chart, which said she had a broken hip the view of the sky over the parking garage the spanish-language newspaper on the tray table the instructions mr. vang read from his tablet "noticing the rosary on the tray table and the spanish-language newspaper," she repeated her introduction in spanish.

what does mrs. ortega's exclamation "¡ay, por fin!" ("oh, finally!") suggest? she is upset that marisol is late. she has wanted someone to speak with her in her own language. she is ready to leave the hospital. she did not understand marisol's english introduction at all. her face changes, she laughs and she begins talking freely. "finally" suggests she had been waiting for someone she could talk to comfortably.

what is the best interpretation of mr. vang's final comment? marisol forgot to fill out the section of the care plan for vital signs. listening showed marisol why patients' own concerns belong in the plan. mr. vang thinks marisol spent too long talking instead of checking vital signs. care plans should be written only in english so every nurse can read them. marisol learned that mrs. ortega's main worry was the walking plan, a patient goal she would never have found by following her clipboard alone.

which inference is best supported by the email? thanh has never received any financial aid from the college before. thanh's spring classes have already been dropped for nonpayment. thanh expects the office may need proof of verification. thanh prefers to be contacted by phone on weekday mornings. thanh attaches a verification receipt, which suggests anticipating a question about whether the documents arrived.

according to the passage, where did the 10,000-step goal originally come from? a federal government health guideline the name of an early japanese pedometer a 2019 study of older women's health a modern fitness tracker company the passage traces the number to a 1960s pedometer called manpo-kei , "10,000-step meter."

according to the passage, what percent of the students who answered the survey said they liked vegetables more? 18% 28% 72% 100% the passage states that 72% of the 180 students said they "liked vegetables more."

what role did james collip play? he came up with the original idea. he purified the extract so it could be used safely. he was the first patient. he bought the patent. the early extracts were impure; collip "found a way to purify the substance."

what can the reader infer from the fact that the team sold the patent for one dollar each? they cared more about access than about profit. they did not think insulin would work. they wanted the university to profit instead. insulin was cheap and easy for the team to produce. they said "insulin belonged to the world," so the token price shows they valued access over personal profit.

what caused the household wells in east porterville to go dry? a broken pipe in the city of porterville's water system drought and heavy pumping that lowered the groundwater farms pumping too much water from rivers and canals a state law that limited the drilling of new wells the passage names years of drought plus increased groundwater pumping by farms with deeper wells as the causes.

based on the passage, why were household wells the first to fail? they were older and more poorly built than the farms' wells. they drew their water from rivers and canals instead of groundwater. they were shallower, so falling groundwater left them dry first. they pumped water faster than the deeper farm wells did. household wells were only 50 to 100 feet deep. as the water table dropped below that, they dried up while deeper farm wells kept pumping.

which detail best shows how residents coped while their wells were dry? the state connected over 700 homes to city water. volunteers set up portable showers at a church. farms drilled deeper wells to reach water. a new law requires agencies to manage groundwater. portable showers at a church show how the community managed day to day while taps were dry.

what can be inferred about the 2014 groundwater law? it targets over-pumping, but full effects will take decades. it quickly ended the east porterville water crisis. it stopped farms from pumping any groundwater. it was passed in response to the 700 home connections in porterville. the law targets over-pumping, a root cause, but "full results are not expected until the 2040s."

based on the passage, at what temperature must supervisors begin giving a 10-minute cool-down rest every two hours? above 80 °f above 95 °f above 100 °f at any temperature the 10-minute cool-down rest is part of the "high-heat procedures" that begin above 95 °f. above 80 °f, shade is required, and water is required at any temperature.

on a 100 °f day, a farmworker becomes confused, slurs his words, and his skin is hot and dry. based on the passage, what is the best response? treat it as heat stroke, a medical emergency, and get emergency help right away. give him a 10-minute rest in the shade and send him back to work. assume he is just tired from a long shift. wait two hours until the next scheduled cool-down break. the passage lists confusion, slurred speech and hot skin that stops sweating as signs of heat stroke, "a medical emergency." the passage calls heat stroke a medical emergency, so waiting, resting or sending him back to work would be unsafe.

to wash your hands, first wet them with clean running water. next, apply soap and lather the backs of your hands, between your fingers, and under your nails. scrub for at least 20 seconds. then rinse well, and finally dry your hands with a clean towel. put the hand-washing steps in order from first to last. wet hands with clean running water apply soap and lather scrub for at least 20 seconds rinse well dry with a clean towel signal words show the order: first (wet), next (soap), scrub 20 seconds, then (rinse), finally (dry).

start with the word heart. remove the letter h. move the t to the front of the word. then change the r to m. what word do the directions produce? team tear heat meat heart without the h is eart. moving the t to the front gives tear. changing the r to m gives team. tear is the trap of stopping one step early.

directions for oral rehydration solution: mix one powder packet into 1 liter of clean water. stir until the powder dissolves. give small sips every few minutes. throw away any unused solution after 24 hours. according to the directions, what should be done with solution that is left after 24 hours? store it in the refrigerator. add a new powder packet to it. throw it away. give it all at once. the last direction says to throw away any unused solution after 24 hours.

to check your blood sugar, wash and dry your hands. insert a test strip into the meter. prick the side of your fingertip with the lancet, and touch the drop of blood to the edge of the strip. wait for the reading, then record it in your log. dispose of the lancet in a sharps container. which step comes immediately after inserting the test strip into the meter? wash and dry the hands well. record the reading in the log. touch the drop of blood to the strip. prick the fingertip with the lancet. the order is: wash hands, insert strip, prick finger, touch blood to strip, read and record, dispose of lancet. touching blood to the strip can't happen until after the finger is pricked.

elena finally received her acceptance letter from the nursing program in june. she had applied in february, right after taking the teas for the second time. her first attempt, the previous november, had left her a few points short in science, so she spent december and january reviewing with a study group. put the events in the order in which they happened, from first to last. elena took the teas for the first time. elena reviewed science with a study group. elena took the teas for the second time. elena applied to the nursing program. elena received her acceptance letter. the passage tells the story out of order, so use the time clues: november (first teas), december–january (study group), february (second teas, then apply), june (acceptance). "right after taking the teas for the second time" shows the second test came just before she applied.

start with the number 12. double it. subtract 4. divide the result by 5. then add 7. what number do the directions produce? 4 11 11.8 5.4 12 doubled is 24; 24 − 4 = 20; 20 ÷ 5 = 4; 4 + 7 = 11. 4 comes from stopping before the last step; 11.8 comes from skipping the subtraction; 5.4 comes from adding 7 before dividing.

write the word nurse. swap the first and last letters. then replace each vowel with the letter that comes right after it in the alphabet. what is the result? nvrsf evrsn fvrsn fursn swapping n and e gives eursn. the vowels are e and u. e becomes f and u becomes v, giving fvrsn. nvrsf forgets the swap; evrsn and fursn each change only one of the two vowels.

medication label: take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with food. do not take with antacids. if you need an antacid, take it at least 2 hours before or 2 hours after this medicine. a patient takes this medicine with breakfast at 8:00 a.m. what is the earliest time after breakfast that she may take an antacid? 8:30 a.m. 10:00 a.m. 9:00 a.m. 12:00 noon the antacid must be at least 2 hours after the medicine: 8:00 a.m. + 2 hours = 10:00 a.m. 8:30 and 9:00 are too soon. noon is allowed but is not the earliest time.

if you see an adult collapse, first make sure the area is safe for you to approach. tap the person's shoulder and shout, "are you okay?" if there is no response, call 911 or have someone else call, and send someone to find an aed. then begin chest compressions right away. put the steps in the order given in the directions. make sure the area is safe. tap the person and shout. call 911 and send someone for an aed. begin chest compressions. the directions use first, then, and "if there is no response" to show the order: check safety, check response, call for help, start compressions.

preparing for your fasting blood test: do not eat or drink anything except water for 10 to 12 hours before your test. for example, if your test is at 7:30 a.m., stop eating by 9:30 p.m. the night before. take your usual medicines with water unless your doctor tells you otherwise. a patient's test is scheduled for 8:00 a.m. based on the directions, what is the latest time she can finish eating the night before? 10:00 p.m. 9:30 p.m. 8:00 p.m. 12:00 midnight she needs at least 10 hours without food. counting back 10 hours from 8:00 a.m. gives 10:00 p.m. 9:30 p.m. is copied from the example, which was for a 7:30 a.m. test. 8:00 p.m. gives 12 hours, which is allowed but is not the latest. midnight gives only 8 hours.

first, preheat the oven to 375 °f. meanwhile, chop the vegetables into bite-sized pieces. after that, toss them with olive oil and salt. finally, roast them for 25 minutes. which word or phrase signals the last step? meanwhile after that first finally "finally" introduces the last step, roasting. "meanwhile" signals something done at the same time as another step, and "after that" signals a middle step.

the ambulance arrived at 2:14 p.m. before it came, a neighbor had found mr. ruiz lying on his porch and started cpr. the neighbor's daughter called 911 while her father did compressions. paramedics then took over and used a defibrillator, and mr. ruiz was breathing on his own by the time he reached the hospital. which event happened first? a neighbor found mr. ruiz on his porch. the neighbor's daughter called 911. the ambulance arrived. paramedics used a defibrillator. the neighbor had to find mr. ruiz before anyone could start cpr or call 911. the passage begins with the ambulance's arrival, but the word "before" shows the earlier events.

gloves go on last so that they cover the cuffs of the gown. before the gloves, put on goggles or a face shield, but only after your mask is in place. the gown is always the first item. a nurse is putting on protective equipment before entering an isolation room. put the items in the order the passage describes, from first to last. gown mask goggles or face shield gloves the gown is "always the first item" and gloves go on "last." goggles go on before the gloves but "only after your mask is in place," so the mask comes second and goggles third.

campus parking rules: students whose first class starts before noon park in lot a. students whose first class starts at noon or later park in lot c. students with a disability placard may use the marked spaces in any lot. ramon's only class on tuesday begins at 1:30 p.m. he does not have a disability placard. where should he park on tuesday? lot a any lot lot c lot b his first (and only) class starts after noon, so the rule sends him to lot c. "any lot" applies only to students with a placard, and lot b is never mentioned.

visitors to the newborn intensive care unit must wash their hands at the sink by the door for 20 seconds and wear a visitor badge at all times. anyone with a fever, cough, or rash must stay home. no more than two visitors may be with a baby at one time. brothers and sisters under age 12 may visit only on sundays. which visitors are following the directions? select all that apply. a grandmother who washes her hands at the door sink before going in a father with a cough who wears a mask during his visit two parents who visit their baby together on a tuesday a 9-year-old brother who visits on a wednesday an aunt who wears her visitor badge during her whole visit washing at the door sink, two visitors at once, and wearing the badge are all allowed. anyone with a cough must stay home; a mask is not an exception. siblings under 12 may visit only on sundays, not wednesdays.

in 1854, cholera swept through the soho neighborhood of london. physician john snow marked on a map the homes of people who had died and noticed that they clustered around a water pump on broad street. he persuaded local officials to remove the pump's handle, and the outbreak soon ended. later, investigators found that a nearby cesspool had been leaking into the well. put the events in the order in which they happened. cholera spread through soho. snow mapped the homes of people who died. officials removed the pump handle. the outbreak ended. investigators found the leaking cesspool. the passage tells these events in order: outbreak, mapping, removing the handle, the outbreak ending, and "later" the discovery of the leak.

how to use your inhaler: shake the inhaler for 5 seconds. breathe out all the way. place the mouthpiece in your mouth, press down once, and breathe in slowly. hold your breath for 10 seconds. if a second puff is prescribed, wait 1 minute before repeating these steps. according to the directions, how long should a patient wait before taking a second puff? 5 seconds 1 minute 10 seconds 1 hour the last direction says to wait 1 minute before repeating. 5 seconds is for shaking and 10 seconds is for holding the breath.

a student wrote these steps for taking a radial pulse: (1) count the beats for 30 seconds. (2) place two fingers on the inside of the wrist, below the thumb. (3) multiply the count by 2. (4) record the pulse rate. which change would put the steps in the correct order? move step 4 so that it comes before step 3. move step 3 so that it comes before step 1. switch steps 3 and 4. move step 2 so that it comes before step 1. you cannot count beats until your fingers are on the pulse, so finding the pulse (step 2) must come first. multiplying must follow counting, and recording should come last, so steps 3 and 4 are already in the right order.

write the word spots. reverse the order of its letters. if the new word has more than four letters, remove its last letter; if it does not, add an e to the end. then change the second letter to h. what word do the directions produce? shot shop shops stop spots reversed is stops. stops has five letters, so remove the last letter: stop. changing the second letter (t) to h gives shop. shot comes from forgetting to reverse; shops skips removing a letter; stop skips the last step.

return your completed form to the front desk. if you are under 18, a parent or guardian must sign section c. if you do not have health insurance, skip section d and go on to section e. a 17-year-old patient has health insurance. which statement about her form is correct? a parent must sign section c, and she should complete section d. she should skip section d because she is under 18. she may sign section c herself because she has insurance. she should give the form to the nurse instead of the front desk. because she is under 18, a parent or guardian signs section c. only patients without insurance skip section d, so she completes it. all forms go to the front desk.

use the medicine label. a 10-year-old needs this medicine. click the line that tells how much to give. a 10-year-old falls in the 6 to 11 years group, so the dose is 1 tablet every 6 hours. the 12-and-over line is a trap: 10 is less than 12. the last line is a limit for everyone, but it doesn't give the dose.

to make a follow-up appointment, students should first log in to the student health portal. next, choose "appointments" from the menu. then select a provider and an open time. finally, click "confirm" and watch for an email. put the steps in order. log in to the portal choose "appointments" select a provider and time click "confirm" signal words show the order: first, next, then, finally.

directions for a urine specimen: wash your hands. open the sterile cup without touching the inside. clean the area with the towelette from front to back. begin urinating into the toilet, then collect the midstream portion in the cup. close the lid and wash your hands again. what should the patient do right after cleaning the area with the towelette? open the sterile cup without touching inside begin urinating into the toilet close the lid wash hands again with soap and water the step after cleaning is to begin urinating into the toilet before collecting the midstream portion.

to renew your parking permit: (1) pay any unpaid citations. (2) log in to the parking website. (3) enter your license plate number. (4) pay the $40 fee. permits cannot be renewed while citations are unpaid. a student logs in and finds she has an unpaid ticket. what should she do? pay the unpaid citation before renewing enter her plate number and pay the $40 fee pay the $40 fee first, then the citation renew now and pay the ticket within 30 days step 1 is to pay unpaid citations, and the last sentence says permits can't be renewed while any are unpaid.

fire drill procedure: when the alarm sounds, stop work and close windows if you can do so in 10 seconds or less. leave lights on. close but do not lock the door. exit by the nearest stairway, never the elevator. meet your group at the flagpole and wait for a head count. which action does not follow the procedure? closing the door without locking it taking the elevator because it is faster leaving the lights on waiting at the flagpole for a head count the procedure says to use the stairs, never the elevator.

according to the flowchart, what should a nurse do if her hands are not visibly dirty and the patient is not on contact precautions for c. diff? wash with soap and water for 20 seconds use alcohol hand rub put on gloves without cleaning hands skip hand hygiene follow the "no" arrows: hands not visibly dirty → no; patient not on c. diff precautions → no. that path ends at "use alcohol hand rub (20–30 s)."

a nurse's hands look clean, and she is about to care for a patient on contact precautions for c. diff. according to the flowchart, what should she do? use alcohol hand rub for 20–30 seconds wash with soap and water for 20 seconds use alcohol hand rub, then wash with soap and water nothing, because her hands look clean first decision: hands not visibly dirty → no, so move down to the second question. second decision: patient on c. diff precautions → yes → wash with soap and water. (c. diff spores aren't killed by alcohol, so they must be washed off. that is the reason for this branch.)

what is the main purpose of the diamond shapes in the flowchart? they show yes-or-no questions where the path splits. they show the steps that take the longest. they mark the final action to take. they show warnings about infections. in a flowchart, a diamond is a decision point: it asks a yes-or-no question, and an arrow leaves for each answer. rectangles show actions or steps. here the green and blue rectangles are the final actions. teas questions about graphics often ask what a shape, color or symbol means. look at how it is used.

what did mai do immediately after giving mr. ibarra his pain medicine? she helped mrs. okafor to the bathroom. she finished her first round of assessments. she made a note to check on him again in an hour. she walked from room to room with carla. paragraph 2: she gave the medicine, then "made a note to come back in an hour." walking rounds with carla and finishing assessments came before the medicine; helping mrs. okafor happened hours later, at 2:30 a.m.

which of these events happened last? pasteur and koch showed that microorganisms cause disease. investigations linked cholera outbreaks to drinking water. most doctors believed that disease spread through bad air. cities began treating drinking water with chlorine. order in the passage: miasma belief (early 1800s), cholera investigations (1850s), germ theory (1860s–1880s), chlorine treatment (early 1900s).

a student attended another college before transferring. to be sure her transcript arrives before the application deadline, by about when should she request it? on february 28 in the middle of february after she receives an email in april by the end of january transcripts take three to four weeks to arrive, and applications close february 28. counting back four weeks from february 28 lands at about the end of january. requesting in mid-february or on february 28 could make the transcript late, and april is long after the deadline.

according to the directions, which action is the last one needed to make the online application complete? uploading the teas score report requesting official transcripts paying the $20 application fee attending the june orientation step 4 says the fee is paid at the end of the form and that the application "is not complete until the fee is paid." orientation happens only after a student is accepted, so it is not part of completing the application.

put these steps in the order the passage gives them. wash your hands with soap and water boil the water if it may not be safe, then cool it pour the water into a clean container add level spoonfuls of sugar and salt shake or stir until everything dissolves the numbered steps give the order: wash hands (1), make the water safe (2), pour it into a container (3), add sugar and salt (4), then mix (5).

a parent made a batch of solution at 9:00 a.m. monday. according to the passage, when should any leftover be thrown away? 9:00 p.m. monday 9:00 a.m. tuesday 9:00 a.m. wednesday when the container is empty leftover solution must be thrown away after 24 hours. 24 hours after 9:00 a.m. monday is 9:00 a.m. tuesday.

after being turned down eleven times, what did hernández do first, according to the passage? he learned russian and earned his pilot's license. he flew aboard the space shuttle discovery to the station. he studied what successful applicants had in common. he earned a master's degree in engineering. "instead of quitting, he studied what successful applicants had in common." the license, scuba and russian came from that study.

put these actions in the order the passage says to do them. avoid caffeine and exercise for 30 minutes sit with your back supported and feet flat wrap the cuff around your bare upper arm sit quietly for 5 minutes take a second reading 1 minute later the headings give the order: before you measure, position, cuff, measure (rest 5 minutes, then two readings), record.

a patient has just walked up three flights of stairs while drinking coffee. according to the passage, what should the patient do? measure right away so the reading is fresh wait 30 minutes before measuring take the reading over a sleeve to save time take only one reading instead of two the passage says not to exercise or drink caffeine for 30 minutes before measuring. waiting 30 minutes follows that direction.

which reading should lead the patient to call the provider, according to the passage? 128/82 on one reading 150/95 on two readings 182/100 on two readings 118/76 on two readings the call rule is a top number of 180 or higher or a bottom number of 120 or higher on two readings. 182 meets the top-number limit on two readings.

put these steps in the order a visitor should follow them. check in at the front desk for a badge call the icu from the phone outside the doors clean your hands with foam beside the door put on a gown and gloves if a yellow sign is posted the guidelines go in order: arrive and check in, call from outside the doors, then clean your hands before entering, and gown up only if a yellow sign is posted.

a family of three adults arrives at 3:00 p.m. according to the guidelines, how many can be at the bedside? none one two three 3:00 p.m. falls during quiet hours (2:00–4:00 p.m.), when one adult visitor may stay.

a visitor brings a small potted plant as a gift. what should happen according to the guidelines? it may stay on the windowsill if the patient agrees. it is not allowed because plants can carry bacteria. it must be checked and cleaned at the front desk first. it is allowed in the room only during quiet hours. "flowers and plants are not allowed because they can carry bacteria."

according to the passage, what should staff do first if the refrigerator temperature goes out of range? throw the vaccines away to protect patients move the vaccines to a freezer to keep them safe call the manufacturer before touching the vaccines label them "do not use" and keep them refrigerated the passage lists labeling them "do not use" and keeping them refrigerated, then calling for advice. it warns against throwing them out too soon.

a patient visited the clinic 35 days ago and has never activated the portal. based on the instructions, what should she expect? her code will still work if she types it exactly as printed. she must wait until her next clinic visit before she can sign up. her code has likely expired, so she may need a new one. she can skip the code and sign up using only her birth date. codes expire 30 days after the visit, and 35 days have passed. calling the help line would be a logical next step.

whole milk (% daily value) nutrition facts serving size 1 cup (240 ml) servings per container 4 calories 150 total fat 8 g 10% saturated fat 5 g 25% sodium 105 mg 5% total carbohydrate 12 g 4% protein 8 g calcium 260 mg 20% according to the label, how many calories are in the entire container? 150 300 600 450 each serving has 150 calories, and there are 4 servings in the container. 150 × 4 = 600 calories. 150 is the trap of reading only one serving.

whole milk (% daily value) nutrition facts serving size 1 cup (240 ml) servings per container 4 calories 150 total fat 8 g 10% saturated fat 5 g 25% sodium 105 mg 5% total carbohydrate 12 g 4% protein 8 g calcium 260 mg 20% which nutrient provides the greatest percent daily value in one serving? total fat calcium sodium saturated fat compare the % daily value column: saturated fat 25%, calcium 20%, total fat 10%, sodium 5%. saturated fat has the highest percentage, even though total fat has more grams.

route 9 northbound, weekdays transit center city college medical center northgate mall 6:00 a.m. 6:10 a.m. 6:22 a.m. 6:35 a.m. 6:30 a.m. 6:40 a.m. 6:52 a.m. 7:05 a.m. 7:00 a.m. 7:10 a.m. 7:22 a.m. 7:35 a.m. 7:30 a.m. 7:40 a.m. 7:52 a.m. 8:05 a.m. a student must be at the medical center by 7:30 a.m. for clinicals. she boards the bus at city college. what is the latest bus she can take from city college? 6:40 a.m. 7:40 a.m. 7:10 a.m. 7:00 a.m. the 7:10 a.m. bus from city college reaches the medical center at 7:22 a.m., before 7:30. the next bus (7:40 a.m.) does not reach the medical center until 7:52, too late. 6:40 works but is not the latest, and 7:00 a.m. is the transit center time.

route 9 northbound, weekdays transit center city college medical center northgate mall 6:00 a.m. 6:10 a.m. 6:22 a.m. 6:35 a.m. 6:30 a.m. 6:40 a.m. 6:52 a.m. 7:05 a.m. 7:00 a.m. 7:10 a.m. 7:22 a.m. 7:35 a.m. 7:30 a.m. 7:40 a.m. 7:52 a.m. 8:05 a.m. how long does the bus ride take from the transit center to northgate mall? 35 minutes 22 minutes 25 minutes 30 minutes every bus leaves the transit center on the hour or half hour and reaches northgate 35 minutes later (for example, 6:00 to 6:35).

contents chapter title page 1 cells and tissues 1 2 the skeletal system 24 3 the muscular system 51 4 the nervous system 77 5 the cardiovascular system 104 on which pages would a student most likely find information about the femur (thigh bone)? pages 1–23 pages 51–76 pages 77–103 pages 24–50 the femur is a bone, so it belongs in chapter 2, the skeletal system. chapter 2 starts on page 24 and ends just before chapter 3 begins on page 51.

index blood pressure, 212–218    high (hypertension), 215–217    measuring, 213    in children, 218 blood types, 230–233 bones. see skeletal system brain, 140–162 a student wants to learn how blood pressure is measured. which page should she turn to first? 212 213 215 230 under "blood pressure," the subentry "measuring" points to page 213. page 212 starts the general topic, page 215 covers hypertension, and page 230 is about blood types.

index blood pressure, 212–218    high (hypertension), 215–217    measuring, 213    in children, 218 blood types, 230–233 bones. see skeletal system brain, 140–162 what does the entry "bones. see skeletal system" tell the reader? page numbers for bones are listed under "skeletal system." the book does not include any information about bones. bones are discussed on the same pages as blood types, 230–233. the skeletal system is covered in the first chapter of the book. a "see" reference sends the reader to a different index entry where the page numbers are listed. it does not mean the topic is missing, and it says nothing about chapter order.

valley pharmacy patient j. morales drug amoxicillin 500 mg capsules directions take 1 capsule by mouth every 8 hours until all are gone. may take with or without food. quantity 30 capsules refills 0 warning may cause diarrhea. if the patient takes the medicine exactly as directed, how many days will the prescription last? 8 days 15 days 10 days 30 days every 8 hours means 24 ÷ 8 = 3 capsules a day. 30 capsules ÷ 3 per day = 10 days. 8 days is the trap of using the hour number.

valley pharmacy patient j. morales drug amoxicillin 500 mg capsules directions take 1 capsule by mouth every 8 hours until all are gone. may take with or without food. quantity 30 capsules refills 0 warning may cause diarrhea. which statement is true according to the label? the capsules must be taken with food. the capsules should be taken every 6 hours. the patient should stop when he feels better. the prescription cannot be refilled. the label lists 0 refills. it says "with or without food," "every 8 hours," and "until all are gone," so the other choices contradict the label.

clinic hours (a.m. hours begin at 8; p.m. hours end at 5) provider specialty mon tue wed thu fri a. nguyen, np family medicine 8–12 1–5 8–5 — 8–12 r. patel, md pediatrics 1–5 8–12 — 8–5 1–5 l. ortiz, pa women's health — 8–5 1–5 1–5 8–12 a parent must bring her child to the pediatrics provider. she can come only before noon, and she works every tuesday. which day should she choose? monday thursday tuesday friday r. patel is the pediatrics provider. patel has morning hours on tuesday (8–12) and thursday (8–5). the parent works tuesdays, so thursday is the only choice. on monday and friday, patel sees patients only from 1 to 5, in the afternoon.

clinic hours (a.m. hours begin at 8; p.m. hours end at 5) provider specialty mon tue wed thu fri a. nguyen, np family medicine 8–12 1–5 8–5 — 8–12 r. patel, md pediatrics 1–5 8–12 — 8–5 1–5 l. ortiz, pa women's health — 8–5 1–5 1–5 8–12 which provider or providers see patients on friday afternoon? a. nguyen only l. ortiz only a. nguyen and l. ortiz r. patel only on friday, nguyen and ortiz work 8–12 (mornings only). patel works 1–5, the only afternoon hours.

in a patient handout about a new medicine, the words do not drive after taking this medicine appear in bold type. what is the most likely reason the writer used bold type? to show the beginning of a new chapter to mark a word that is defined in the glossary to call attention to an important warning to show that the words are a quotation writers use bold type to make key information, such as safety warnings, stand out. quotations use quotation marks, and a single bold sentence in a handout does not mark a chapter or a glossary word.

a student needs to quickly find the meaning of the word homeostasis in her biology textbook. which part of the book would be most useful? the table of contents the glossary the bibliography the preface a glossary is an alphabetical list of key terms with their definitions. the table of contents lists chapters, the bibliography lists sources, and the preface introduces the book.

use the map. a patient leaves the clinic and walks straight to the pharmacy. in which direction does she walk? northeast northwest southeast southwest the compass arrow points up, so up is north and right is east. the pharmacy is up and to the right of the clinic, which is northeast.

use the map and its scale bar. the distance from the center of the library to the center of the clinic is twice the length of the scale bar. about how far is the library from the clinic? 0.5 mile 1.5 miles 1 mile 2 miles the scale bar stands for 0.5 mile. two scale-bar lengths = 2 × 0.5 = 1 mile. 0.5 mile is the trap of reading the bar's label without multiplying.

overnight oats (makes 2 servings) 1 cup rolled oats 1 cup milk ½ cup plain yogurt 1 tablespoon honey ½ cup berries directions: mix all ingredients except the berries in a jar. refrigerate for at least 6 hours. top with the berries just before serving. a student wants to make 4 servings. how much milk will she need? 1 cup 2 cups 1½ cups 4 cups the recipe makes 2 servings, so 4 servings means doubling everything. 1 cup × 2 = 2 cups. 4 cups is the trap of using one cup per serving.

overnight oats (makes 2 servings) 1 cup rolled oats 1 cup milk ½ cup plain yogurt 1 tablespoon honey ½ cup berries directions: mix all ingredients except the berries in a jar. refrigerate for at least 6 hours. top with the berries just before serving. according to the recipe, when should the berries be added? before refrigerating after 2 hours in the refrigerator while mixing the oats and milk just before serving the directions say to mix everything except the berries and to top with them "just before serving."

a pamphlet about type 2 diabetes has the following headings: i. what is type 2 diabetes? ii. who is at risk? iii. ______ iv. how is type 2 diabetes treated? which heading best fits in the blank? how is type 2 diabetes diagnosed? the history of insulin research recipes for a healthy thanksgiving how the heart pumps blood the headings move logically from what the disease is, to who gets it, to finding it, to treating it. diagnosis fits between risk and treatment. the other headings are off topic or out of place in this sequence.

drug facts active ingredient (in each tablet) ibuprofen 200 mg uses temporarily relieves minor aches and pains, headache, and toothache; temporarily reduces fever directions: adults and children 12 years and older take 1 tablet every 4 to 6 hours while symptoms last. if pain or fever does not respond to 1 tablet, 2 tablets may be used. do not take more than 6 tablets in 24 hours unless directed by a doctor. children under 12 years ask a doctor which statements are supported by the label? select all that apply. an adult may take 2 tablets at once if 1 tablet does not help. an adult may take up to 6 tablets in 24 hours without asking a doctor. a 10-year-old should take 1 tablet every 6 hours. the medicine can be used to lower a fever. an adult may take 1 tablet every 2 hours. the label allows 2 tablets if 1 does not work, a maximum of 6 in 24 hours, and lists "reduces fever" under uses. children under 12 should "ask a doctor," so no dose is given for a 10-year-old. doses are every 4 to 6 hours, not every 2 hours.

the guide words at the top of a dictionary page are lumbar and lymph . which word would appear on this page? lucid lumbago lung lymphoma words on the page fall alphabetically between the two guide words. "lung" (l-u-n) comes after "lumbar" (l-u-m) and before "lymph" (l-y). "lucid" (l-u-c) and "lumbago" (l-u-m-b-a-g, and g comes before r) come before "lumbar"; "lymphoma" comes after "lymph."

use the table of contents. click the chapter that most likely explains how to throw away a used needle. in health care, sharps are needles, lancets, scalpels and anything else that can cut or puncture skin. "disposing" means throwing away, so chapter 4 is the place to look. use headings and tables of contents to find information quickly instead of reading everything.

a textbook chapter has the heading "chapter 9: the respiratory system" and the subheading "9.3 gas exchange in the alveoli." what is the purpose of the subheading? to give the main topic of the entire chapter to show the specific topic of that section to summarize the conclusion of the section to define the term "alveoli" for the reader the chapter heading names the broad topic; a numbered subheading names the narrower topic of one section.

in a textbook, the word homeostasis appears in bold italic type the first time it is used. what does this text feature most likely signal? it is a word borrowed from another language. it is the title of a book or journal article. it is a direct quotation taken from another source. it is a key term defined nearby or in the glossary. textbooks put key vocabulary in bold (often with italics) the first time it appears, then define it nearby or in the glossary.

where should a reader look to quickly find every page that mentions "insulin" in a biology textbook? the table of contents the index the glossary the preface an index lists specific terms alphabetically with every page number where they appear.

a health brochure includes a sidebar titled "myth vs. fact" in a shaded box. what is the most likely purpose of the sidebar? to present the brochure's main argument and evidence to quickly correct common misunderstandings to define technical terms used in the brochure to compare two treatment options side by side sidebars present extra information apart from the main text. a myth-versus-fact box corrects misunderstandings at a glance.

a patient's daughter wants to know whether her 8-year-old son can visit. according to the table of contents, on which page should she start reading? page 5 page 9 page 17 page 31 chapter 3, "visitors: hours, children and quiet time," names children in its title. it begins on page 9.

a patient wants to know how to ask for a payment plan for his hospital bill. which chapter is most likely to have this information? chapter 5, your rights and responsibilities chapter 8, going home: discharge planning chapter 9, paying for your care the index, page 42 a payment plan is about paying the bill, so chapter 9, "paying for your care," is the most direct match. the index might list "payment plans," but it would only send the reader back into a chapter, most likely chapter 9.

a patient wants to know whether he can keep his insulin in a hot car. which page of the book should he turn to first? 41 44 47 50 the question is about where to keep insulin, so look under the main entry "insulin" for the subentry "storing." "storing" is on page 47.

a parent reads pages 58–63 about low blood sugar but wants more detail on what to give her child during a low. based on the index, what should she look up next? the main entry "glucose tablets" insulin, pumps ketones insulin, injection sites "see also" sends the reader to a related entry with more information. under "treating," the index says "see also glucose tablets." "see" (without "also") is different: it means the information is listed under another name, as with "ketones. see diabetic ketoacidosis."
according to the label, how many capsules should maria take in one day? 1 2 3 8 the label says 1 capsule every 8 hours. a day has 24 hours, and 24 ÷ 8 = 3, so she takes 3 capsules a day.

maria takes her first capsule at 7:00 a.m. following the label, when should she take her next dose? 11:00 a.m. 1:00 p.m. 3:00 p.m. 7:00 p.m. "every 8 hours" means 8 hours after the last dose. 7:00 a.m. + 8 hours = 3:00 p.m. the next one would be 11:00 p.m.

which statements are supported by the prescription label? select all that apply. maria should keep taking the capsules even after she feels better. maria can get this prescription refilled once. the capsules should not be taken after march 14. the medicine may affect how well some birth control pills work. the yellow warning says to finish all of the medicine, so she should keep taking it after she feels better. "discard after: 03/14" means don't use it after march 14, and the red sticker warns about birth control pills. the label says refills: none, so she cannot refill it.

a fire alarm sounds while you are at the spot marked "you are here." using the map and its legend, click the emergency exit you can reach most quickly. the legend shows the star means "you are here" and green boxes are emergency exits. you are in exam rooms 5–8, and one exit is right in the bottom wall of that area, much closer than walking down the hallway to either end. map questions on the teas test whether you use the legend (key) and read positions carefully.

according to the floor plan, which room is directly across the hallway from the nurses' station? pharmacy lab x-ray waiting room the nurses' station is in the bottom row, in the middle-left section. directly above it, across the hallway, is the lab.

a visitor in the waiting room needs a fire extinguisher. based on the map, where is the only one shown? next to the right-end exit at the left end of the hallway inside the x-ray room next to the nurses' station the legend shows a fire extinguisher as a small red cylinder. the only one on the map is at the left end of the hallway, near the left exit.

a reader wants to know what to do on a windy, dusty day. under which heading should she look? what is it? lowering your risk symptoms who is at higher risk? the "lowering your risk" section gives advice for windy, dusty days, such as staying indoors and wearing an n95.

a reader wants to know whether she should stop drinking coffee in the afternoon. which section should she read? the sleep cycle what sleep does when sleep runs short better sleep habits the "better sleep habits" section recommends avoiding caffeine in the afternoon.

why are the application dates printed in bold type? to show that the dates are a quotation to draw attention to an important deadline to mark the title of a new chapter to show that the dates may change bold type makes key information stand out. the application window is critical because late applications are not reviewed.

according to the label, what is the greatest number of milligrams of ibuprofen an adult should take in 24 hours without a doctor's direction? 200 mg 400 mg 1,200 mg 2,400 mg the limit is 6 tablets in 24 hours, and each tablet has 200 mg: 6 × 200 mg = 1,200 mg.

which people does the label say have a higher chance of stomach bleeding? select all that apply. a 64-year-old who takes the tablets as directed a person who has had a stomach ulcer a 30-year-old who takes the tablets with milk a person who takes a blood thinner a person who has 1 glass of wine with dinner the stomach bleeding warning lists age 60 or older, past ulcers or bleeding, blood thinners or steroids, 3 or more drinks a day, and taking more or longer than directed. taking it with milk is allowed, and one drink a day is below the "3 or more" in the warning.

a 15-year-old has had a fever for 4 days while taking this product as directed. based on the label, what should happen next? take 2 tablets instead of 1 stop use and ask a doctor keep taking it for up to 10 days switch to taking it only with food the label says to stop use and ask a doctor if fever lasts more than 3 days. four days is more than 3.

why does the label define nsaid in small print under the active ingredient? to advertise that the product is stronger than other pain relievers to prove that the product has been tested by doctors to explain a term the reader needs in order to understand the warning to show that the product does not cause stomach problems the stomach bleeding warning says "this product contains an nsaid." defining the term first helps the reader connect the warning to this product. a label's text features (headings, tables, footnotes) organize safety information; they don't advertise or prove anything.

a visitor is going to see a patient in room 512. where should the visitor go after checking in? floor 5, south tower floor 5, north tower floor 4, north tower floor 3, south tower rooms 501–520 are in pediatrics, floor 5 of the north tower.

a family member in the surgery waiting room wants to walk to the laboratory without going outside. which route is the most direct one that matches the directory? take the floor 2 skybridge straight across to the north tower take the floor 3 skybridge to the north tower leave through the elm st. entrance and walk to the north tower take the floor 5 skybridge to the north tower the surgery waiting room is on floor 2 south, and the laboratory is on floor 2 north. the towers connect on floor 2, so the skybridge goes straight across.

what does the asterisk (*) in the directory tell the reader? the unit is closed to all visitors at all times. the unit is located in the basement of the north tower. visitors must call from outside the doors before entering. the unit can only be reached by taking a skybridge. the note at the bottom matches the asterisk: "visitors must call from the phone outside the unit doors before entering."

a visitor arrives at 7:00 a.m., goes straight to the icu, and is turned away at the door. which step did the visitor most likely skip? eating breakfast at the cafeteria before going up to the unit checking in at the desk and calling before entering entering the hospital through the elm st. emergency entrance taking the floor 2 skybridge instead of the floor 4 skybridge the directory says to check in at the information desk for a badge before going to any unit, and the icu's asterisk means visitors must call before entering.

which applicant meets all of the required qualifications? a high school graduate with a cna certificate who can lift 50 lb with assistance but has no cpr card a ged holder with a cna certificate and a current bls card who can lift 50 lb with assistance an lvn student who speaks spanish and has a bls card and a diploma but no cna certificate a cna with 2 years of long-term care experience and a bls card but no diploma or ged the required column lists four items: cna certificate, bls card, lifting 50 lb with assistance, and a diploma or ged. only this applicant has all four.
what is the total hourly pay for this night-shift job, including the night differential? $20.50 $22.50 $24.50 $25.00 $22.50 base + $2.00 night differential = $24.50 per hour.

an employee who starts work on june 1 enrolls in an lvn program. based on the posting, which benefit can the employee use? only medical insurance starting june 1 tuition help of up to $3,000 per year free lvn classes paid in full by the employer a day shift schedule the posting offers tuition help of up to $3,000 per year for employees in nursing programs. insurance starts after 60 days, not on day one.

under which heading would a reader find what to have ready before signing up? steps before you begin important need help? the "before you begin" list names the activation code, date of birth and email.

why is the sentence about codes expiring printed in bold? it explains how to get a new code. it is an important warning the reader could easily miss. it marks the start of a new section. it tells readers that this step is optional for some patients. bold type draws attention to key warnings. if the code expires, the patient can't sign up, so the writers made sure it stands out.

what is the purpose of the box outlined in red? to warn that the portal is not for emergencies to list what to have ready before signing up to explain how to get help with the portal by phone to warn that activation codes expire the red outline and "important" label set apart a safety warning: emergencies need 911 or an emergency room, not a portal message.

children in the united states usually receive the mmr vaccine in two doses. the first dose is given at 12 to 15 months of age, and the second at 4 to 6 years. the vaccine protects against three diseases: measles, mumps, and rubella. what is the author's main purpose? to persuade parents to refuse the mmr vaccine to inform readers about when children receive the mmr vaccine to entertain readers with a story about a child's checkup to express the author's fear of measles the passage gives facts (doses, ages, diseases) without opinions or a story, so its purpose is to inform. it does not argue against vaccines, tell a story, or share feelings.

every student on this campus deserves a quiet place to study between classes. the library closes at 6 p.m., yet many of us work during the day and take evening classes. i urge the student senate to keep at least one floor of the library open until 10 p.m. what is the author's primary purpose? to persuade the student senate to extend library hours to inform readers about the history of the library to describe the evening classes offered on campus to entertain readers with a story about studying "i urge the student senate" is a call to action, which signals a persuasive purpose. the passage gives no library history, does not describe classes, and tells no story.

on my first day as a hospital volunteer, i proudly pushed a patient's wheelchair down the hall and straight into the supply closet. the patient laughed so hard that she asked me to do it again on the way back. what is the author's main purpose? to teach readers how to push a wheelchair safely to persuade students to volunteer at hospitals to inform readers about the layout of a hospital to entertain readers with a funny story the passage is a short, humorous personal story, and its goal is to amuse. it gives no instructions, makes no argument, and does not describe the hospital's layout.

you will probably feel nervous before your first clinical rotation. your hands may shake as you take your first blood pressure. remember that your instructor expects you to be learning, not to be perfect. from which point of view is the passage written? first person second person third person limited third person omniscient the author speaks directly to the reader using "you" and "your," which is second person. first person would use "i" or "we"; third person would use "he," "she," or "they."

some people say the planned freeway expansion will cut commute times. perhaps it will. but the plan would also bulldoze forty homes in one of fresno's oldest neighborhoods and bring more truck exhaust near two elementary schools. faster commutes are a poor trade for families' homes and children's lungs. which statement best describes the author's point of view? the author supports the freeway expansion. the author has no opinion about the freeway expansion. the author opposes the freeway expansion. the author is mainly concerned about commute times. the author admits the expansion might shorten commutes, then argues that the costs to homes and health are too high. the last sentence, "a poor trade," clearly shows opposition.

(1) most people think of bones as dry, lifeless sticks. (2) in fact, bone is living tissue that constantly breaks down and rebuilds itself. (3) cells called osteoclasts dissolve old bone, while osteoblasts lay down new bone. (4) this ongoing process is what allows a broken bone to heal. why does the author most likely include sentence 1? to introduce a common belief that the passage will correct to explain how osteoclasts dissolve old bone tissue to persuade readers to drink more milk for strong bones to state the main idea that the rest of the passage supports sentence 1 states a common idea, and "in fact" in sentence 2 corrects it. the main idea, that bone is living tissue, is in sentence 2, not sentence 1. osteoclasts are explained in sentence 3, and milk is never mentioned.

it is shameful that, in one of the richest farming regions on earth, many of the families who harvest our food still struggle to afford groceries. we should not accept this. which word best describes the author's tone? amused neutral hopeful indignant words like "shameful" and "we should not accept this" show anger at an unfair situation, which is an indignant tone. nothing is funny, the language is not neutral, and the author expresses outrage rather than hope.

an author writes a brochure for a dialysis center that explains what new patients can expect at their first appointment. what is the author's primary purpose? to inform to entertain to express personal feelings to persuade patients to switch centers explaining what to expect gives readers information, so the purpose is to inform. a brochure for the same center would not urge patients to go elsewhere.

telehealth visits saved many patients a long drive during the pandemic, and for routine follow-ups they remain a sensible choice. but a video screen cannot replace a nurse's hands. a swollen ankle, a faint rash, or the smell of an infected wound can be missed when a patient is seen only through a camera. which statement would the author most likely agree with? telehealth visits should no longer be offered to patients. video visits are better than office visits for spotting rashes and swelling. telehealth is useful for some visits but should not replace all in-person exams. most patients would rather drive long distances than use telehealth for visits. the author calls telehealth "sensible" for routine follow-ups but warns about what it can miss. the author does not want to end telehealth, says video visits can miss rashes, and never says patients prefer long drives.

the waiting room was crowded, and mrs. flores clutched her purse. she had not seen a doctor in five years, and she wondered whether the nurse would scold her. when the nurse smiled and said, "i'm so glad you came in," mrs. flores felt her shoulders relax. from whose point of view is the passage told? mrs. flores herself, describing her visit in the first person a third-person narrator who shares mrs. flores's thoughts the nurse, describing mrs. flores in the first person a narrator who speaks directly to the reader, using "you" throughout the narrator uses "she" and "her" (third person) and tells us what mrs. flores wonders and feels. there is no "i" narrator, and the reader is never addressed as "you." the nurse's words are quoted, but the story is not told by the nurse.

an article about heat illness begins with a short story about a young farmworker who collapsed in a vineyard on a 108 °f afternoon. what is the most likely reason the author begins this way? to prove that every farmworker will develop heat illness to entertain readers with a humorous anecdote to give statistics about how often heat illness occurs in california to capture readers' interest and show the real danger of the topic opening with a real-life-style story is a common way to hook readers and make a danger feel personal. one story cannot prove what happens to every worker, the story is not funny, and a story is not a statistic.

a visit to an urgent care center for a minor sprain usually costs a fraction of what the same care costs in an emergency room, and the wait is often much shorter. for problems that are not life-threatening, urgent care is often the better choice. chest pain, trouble breathing, or signs of a stroke, however, always call for the er. what is the author's main purpose? to persuade readers never to visit the emergency room to complain about long waits in emergency rooms to explain how emergency rooms and urgent care centers are paid for to help readers decide when to use urgent care instead of the er the author compares the two options and tells readers which situations fit each one. the author says some problems always need the er, so "never" is wrong. waits are mentioned as a reason, not as a complaint, and funding is not discussed.

my grandmother's hands were rough from forty summers in the vineyards near selma, but they were the gentlest hands i have ever known. whenever i was sick, she would rest one cool palm on my forehead and hum until i fell asleep. what is the author's main purpose? to inform readers about the grape harvest near selma to express love and admiration for her grandmother to persuade readers to care for sick children at home to explain how to treat rough, dry skin the warm memories and words like "gentlest" show that the author is sharing feelings. the vineyards are background, and the passage gives no facts about harvests, no argument, and no skin-care advice.

a pamphlet praising a new sports drink was written and paid for by the company that makes the drink. what is most likely the pamphlet's main purpose? to entertain readers with jokes to compare the drink fairly with water to persuade readers to buy the drink to express the writer's personal feelings a company writing about its own product usually wants readers to buy it. a seller's pamphlet that "praises" the product is not a fair comparison.

should nursing students be allowed to use their phones during clinical rotations? a drug-reference app can answer a question about a medication in seconds. yet a student glancing at a screen might miss a change in a patient's color or breathing. on balance, the answer seems to be yes, but only for reference apps, and only away from the bedside. which statement best describes the author's point of view? the author supports limited phone use during clinicals. the author is completely against phone use during clinicals. the author supports unlimited phone use during clinicals. the author does not take a position on phone use. the author weighs a benefit and a risk, then concludes "yes, but only" in certain conditions. that is a limited yes: not a full ban, not unlimited use, and not neutral.

energy drinks are marketed as a harmless boost for tired students, but the reality is far less cheerful. a single can may contain as much caffeine as three cups of coffee, plus a staggering amount of sugar. students who reach for these sugary jolts night after night may end up jittery, sleepless, and no better prepared for their exams. which phrases from the passage show the author's negative attitude toward energy drinks? select all that apply. "far less cheerful" "a staggering amount of sugar" "these sugary jolts" "tired students" "three cups of coffee" "far less cheerful," "staggering," and "sugary jolts" are word choices that make energy drinks sound bad. "tired students" describes the buyers, and "three cups of coffee" is a neutral comparison of caffeine amounts.

which of the following was most likely written mainly to entertain? a chart comparing average starting pay for nurses in five california cities a letter urging county voters to approve a bond measure for a new children's hospital a short story about a nursing student who adopts a goat during finals week a brochure listing a community clinic's hours, services, and accepted insurance plans a funny short story is written to entertain. a pay chart and a clinic brochure inform, and a letter urging voters persuades.
